title: Weekend Sign Installer - Plainfield, IL
description:
Directed is seeking an independent contractor to place and pick up temporary weekend signs in the Plainfield, IL area in the community Reserve at Springbank.

The contractor will be responsible for installing signs between Friday at 5:00 PM and Saturday at 10:00 AM. The same signs must be picked up between Sunday at 6:00 PM and Monday at 8:00 AM. The work may be performed at any time within those windows, as long as all signs are placed by Saturday at 10:00 AM and removed by Monday at 8:00 AM.

The signs are lightweight corrugated plastic, and are installed on wooden stakes. Artisan Direct provides the signs and stakes and provides replacement inventory as needed.

Job Duties:

  • Use Directed's mobile application to report installation and pickup of signs at specific locations
  • Install signs every weekend between Friday 5 PM and Saturday 10 AM
  • Pickup the same signs between Sunday 6 PM and Monday 8 AM
  • Store signs and extra stakes safely during the week
  • Submit a weekly invoice and order replacement inventory after completing pick up- using our website
Pay Information:
  • Starting compensation is $ 121 per weekend
  • Pay is issued via direct deposit every two weeks
  • $20.00 Signing bonus
  • $100.00 bonus after 4 weeks of completed work

Requirements

  • Valid driver’s license and current auto insurance
  • 18+ years old
  • Reliable vehicle with enough space to transport 30+ signs
  • A smartphone (Android or iPhone), roughly four years old or newer, capable of running our mobile app
  • Ability to lift and place signs and work outdoors
  • Ability to hammer stakes 6–8 inches into the ground during the first weekend only
  • Dependable and able to complete routes within the required time windows each weekend

Independent Contractor Notice

This is a 1099 independent contractor position. Contractors are not employees of Directed and are responsible for their own fuel, expenses, taxes and insurance. Contractors determine their own driving order, provide their own vehicle and mobile device, and complete the work within the placement and pickup windows provided. title: Director, People & Culture
description:
This role is solely based out of Houston, TX and we will only be accepting candidates who live in Houston, TX or the surrounding area

POSITION OVERVIEW

Harbor Health is hiring a Director of People & Culture to lead people strategy for our Houston market and manage HR partnership across our other Texas markets (Austin, El Paso, Dallas, San Antonio).

You're joining at a pivotal moment. Harbor is growing quickly, and Houston is a key part of that growth. The person in this seat will be central to how that growth lands with our teammates. You'll spend real time in clinics, building relationships with physicians and operations leaders, and making sure people feel supported. You'll also manage an HR Employee Relations & Experience Manager covering our other Texas markets, so you'll shape how People & Culture shows up across the state.

This isn't a traditional HR role. We have policies because we need them, and we know people don't fit neatly into policies. You'll be the person managers and clinicians call when something doesn't fit the template. You'll have the judgment to know when to hold the line and when to make an exception, and you'll be able to explain the difference. You'll partner closely with the Chief People Officer, and together we'll build a People & Culture function that people actually want to work with.

POSITION DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Houston Market Partnership

  • Serve as the primary People & Culture partner for physician, clinical, and operations leaders in the Houston market.

  • Be visible and present in clinics, building trust with managers and teammates through direct relationships rather than administering HR from a distance.

  • Support the market through periods of growth and change, coaching managers and making sure people feel informed and supported.

  • Bring the Houston market perspective into company-wide People & Culture conversations.

Team Leadership Across Texas

  • Manage one HR Business Partner supporting Austin, El Paso, Dallas, and San Antonio.

  • Set the bar for how People & Culture shows up in the field: responsive, judgment-driven, close to the business.

  • Partner with the CPO on shared support for corporate functions.

Employee Relations & Judgment Calls

  • Handle complex and sensitive ER matters directly, in partnership with the CPO and legal counsel when needed.

  • Coach managers through hard people conversations rather than always owning them outright, and build manager capability over time.

  • Spot patterns across markets and bring proactive recommendations to the executive team.

Policy, Compliance & Practical Application

  • Provide input on policies that need to evolve, and flag when what's on paper isn't working in practice.

  • Partner with centralized HR Operations on benefits, leaves, accommodations, and compliance, applying policy with judgment in individual cases.

  • Maintain strong working knowledge of Texas employment law and federal regulations (ADA, FMLA, FLSA, Title VII, EEOC).

Culture & Employee Experience

  • Own culture and employee experience strategy for the Houston market in partnership with the CPO.

  • Lead culture integration work related to acquisitions and organizational growth.

  • Use stay interviews, exit interviews, and pulse data to drive real changes, not just report them.

DESIRED PROFESSIONAL SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

Required

  • 8+ years of progressive HR experience, including at least 3 years managing others

  • A track record of being in the field with the business, not running HR from a desk

  • Strong judgment in ambiguous, high-stakes situations, and the ability to explain your reasoning to skeptical audiences

  • Direct experience partnering with physician, clinical, or operations leadership

  • Comfort holding your own with executives, physicians, and front-line teammates in the same day

  • Strong working knowledge of Texas employment law

  • Experience in multi-site, high-growth, or post-acquisition environments

  • Executive presence without corporate stiffness

Preferred

  • Healthcare industry experience, particularly with clinical or physician populations

  • Experience supporting an acquisition or integration

  • Comfort using AI tools like Claude as everyday work accelerators

  • Bilingual English/Spanish

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Competitive total cash compensation plus meaningful equity

  • Generous PTO and 10 paid holidays

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • 401(k) plan

  • A real seat at the table shaping how People & Culture works at a company trying to do healthcare differently

COMPANY OVERVIEW

At Harbor Health, we're transforming healthcare in Texas through collaboration and innovation. As a payvider, we combine comprehensive care with our own health plan to give members a more connected experience. If you're ready to do meaningful work in a place where your judgment and voice matter, we'd love to hear from you.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Harbor Health is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. All employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

title: Client Navigator
description:
Our Vision: A community that prioritizes love, compassion, and equity over judgment, shame, and division.



Client Navigator

Salary Range: $64,360 – $69,464



Kalamazoo Defender is an independent non-profit organization that provides legal representation to the adult indigent population charged with a crime within Kalamazoo County. We take a holistic approach, employing compassionate professionals who work with our clients to identify and address additional needs beyond their legal case. In collaboration with our robust network of area service providers, we aim to connect our clients to relevant support services.

We fight for justice in the courts, care in the community, and dignity in the world. Our mission is rooted in the conviction that poverty and various forms of discrimination put our clients on inequitable footing within and beyond our criminal justice system. Our job is to be their zealous defender in the face of these systemic barriers, fighting for them in court, organizing care for them in our community, and advocating for their inherent dignity in the broader world.



THE JOB:



Kalamazoo Defender seeks a full-time Client Navigator, reporting to the Lead Client Navigator, to provide direct advocacy, resource navigation, and case support to clients as part of our multidisciplinary defense team. Working alongside attorneys, paralegals, investigators, mitigation specialists, and other members of the defense team, Client Navigators help identify and address barriers that may affect a client's stability, well-being, and ability to meaningfully participate in their defense.

Client Navigators spend significant time working directly with clients, including through scheduled appointments, walk-in services, phone communication, and meetings at court or correctional facilities. They work with clients to identify needs and goals, develop individualized action and release plans, connect clients with community-based services and treatment, coordinate assessments and evaluations, advocate with service providers, and support clients in accessing appropriate community resources and services. The work requires proactive communication with clients, community partners, and the legal team so that social-service support and resource navigation complement the client's broader defense strategy.

The ideal candidate is compassionate, resourceful, organized, and solution-oriented and is comfortable working in a highly client-facing environment where needs and priorities may shift throughout the day. This position requires the ability to build trusting relationships with clients who may be experiencing trauma, housing instability, substance use, mental health concerns, disability, poverty, or other significant barriers while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries. Strong communication, follow-through, judgment, initiative, and the ability to navigate complex community systems are essential.



RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Conduct holistic assessments with clients to identify needs, strengths, barriers, available supports, and appropriate next steps for connection to services.

  • Meet and communicate directly with clients in person, by phone, and through other appropriate communication methods to assess needs, provide support, navigate resources, and assist with connection to appropriate services.

  • Participate in rotating Client Navigator walk-in coverage, providing responsive, face-to-face navigation services to eligible clients, including assessment of immediate needs, resource identification, referrals, and connection to community-based services.

  • Work collaboratively with clients to identify goals and develop individualized action plans that reflect client priorities and circumstances.

  • Provide resource navigation, advocacy, and practical support by identifying appropriate services, explaining available options, and assisting clients in accessing community-based resources.

  • Coordinate assessments, evaluations, treatment, housing, benefits, and other services as appropriate to the client's needs and legal circumstances.

  • Develop release plans, action plans, referral summaries, and other client-service documentation needed to support clients and the defense team.

  • Collaborate with attorneys to identify opportunities for case-specific support and ensure Client Navigator services are coordinated with the client's legal representation.

  • Develop and maintain working knowledge of local community resources, programs, eligibility requirements, and referral processes.

  • Proactively communicate and build professional relationships with community-based service providers by phone, email, and in person to make referrals, clarify eligibility, address access barriers, coordinate services, and advocate for clients.

  • Coordinate meetings involving clients, defense team members, treatment providers, and other community partners when necessary to facilitate resource connection, coordination, and access.

  • Maintain accurate, complete, timely, and well-organized case notes and electronic case files documenting identified needs, navigation efforts, referrals, service connections, and outcomes.

  • Learn and effectively use case-management systems and other technology tools necessary to document services, communicate with the defense team, and maintain confidential client information.

  • Support effective resource connection and soft handoffs when clients transition between services, providers, or out of Client Navigator services.

  • Complete and close Client Navigation cases when identified needs have been addressed or appropriate navigation efforts have been completed, while maintaining access to walk-in support as appropriate while the client's Kalamazoo Defender case remains open.

  • Maintain appropriate professional boundaries with clients to support equitable, ethical, and sustainable client services.

  • Respond professionally and compassionately to clients experiencing crisis or heightened emotions, using appropriate communication and de-escalation techniques.

  • Collaborate effectively with attorneys, paralegals, investigators, mitigation specialists, fellow Client Navigators, reception staff, and other members of the multidisciplinary defense team to support holistic, client-centered representation.

  • Travel to courthouses and correctional facilities or other locations as needed to meet with clients and coordinate services.

  • Participate in training and professional development and maintain current knowledge of community resources, service systems, and practices relevant to the role.

  • Perform any other duties as assigned, contributing to the overall effectiveness and success of the defense team.

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree or at least 1–2 years of relevant experience in advocacy, case management, social services, resource navigation, human services, or a related field.

  • Strong commitment to Kalamazoo Defender's mission and values.

  • Ability to work effectively with diverse populations, including individuals with disabilities, those struggling with addiction, and those experiencing mental health crises.

  • Commitment to cultural awareness, maintaining professionalism, ensuring confidentiality, and acting with compassion and integrity.

  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, including the ability to initiate and maintain professional communication with clients, service providers, and community partners in person, by phone, and electronically.

  • Ability to build rapport and maintain appropriate professional boundaries while working in a highly client-facing environment and responding flexibly to both scheduled and unscheduled client needs.

  • Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple clients, appointments, priorities, and deadlines while working both collaboratively and independently.

  • Strong problem-solving and resource-navigation skills, including the ability to identify barriers, explore available options, and help clients navigate complex systems.

  • Ability to manage high-stress or emotionally charged interactions with patience, professionalism, sound judgment, and appropriate de-escalation techniques.

  • Strong documentation and record-keeping skills.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and other basic office technologies and comfort learning and working with new software, systems, and technology tools.

title: Shop Steward
description:
About Tutor

We believe general-purpose, generally-intelligent robots will be built in our lifetimes. Robots will work in our factories, move our goods, walk on our streets and eventually be in our homes. To build that future, research and deployment must work in lockstep: real-world operation must make the technology better and better technology must make deployment easier. We're looking for the thinkers, builders, and researchers who want to be part of that loop.

As an AI robotics company that deploys its inventions directly into the facilities that need them, on state-of-the-art hardware, every robot we build at Tutor has a direct impact on the global, physical economy.

The Role

Our hardware engineers design, build, and test robots in the same building, often in the same afternoon. That only works when the shop works: the part is where the system says it is, the tool is on the wall, and this morning's delivery is already in the building and unpacked, and the space is clean.

We are looking for the person who owns that. You will run the day-to-day of our R&D shop, the Garage: its storage, inventory, tools and equipment, some purchasing, receiving, and layout. You report to the Hardware Engineering Manager. You will work with the Engineering Manager to own and adapt the space as our needs change and grow.

The core idea is simple: things without a home do not get put away. Your first job is to give everything in the shop a home, make it obvious, and keep it true.

Everyone keeps the Garage clean. Engineers own their benches and their messes. You set the standard, keep shared spaces in shape and help others meet the standard.

No degree is required, and you do not need to be an engineer. You do need to be comfortable tinkering and wrenching, and excited to work around 3D printers, electronics, CNC machines, and robots.

Requirements

What you will own

  • Give every tool, part, material, and project a labeled home, and set the pattern engineers copy for their
  • Plan the layout as the team grows; order, receive, and assemble furniture, workbenches, and racks.
  • Have tools, a computer, a desk, and a workspace ready for every new engineer on day one.
  • Buy shop supplies and keep consumables stocked before anyone is blocked.
  • Manage the reciept of larger orders like furniture or components that come crated or on pallets
  • Keep tools organized and working, and maintain the 3D printers, CNC machine, and other shop equipment.
  • Willingness to run the CNC occasionally for small jobs. We will teach you.
  • Set a clear, visible cleanliness standard with simple daily or weekly routines the whole team follows.
  • Keep shared areas, storage, and the robot testing space clean yourself, and nudge people back to the standard. When something keeps getting left out, fix its home first.
  • Purge hardware we no longer need on a regular schedule: confirm with the owning engineer, sell what has value, recycle the rest.
  • Manage teardown of retired robots, recovering the parts worth keeping.
  • Handle scrap, recycling, and removal of bulk material like crates, pallets, and scrap metal.

    • Who you are

    • Extremely organized and detail-oriented.
    • Hands-on. You would rather build the shelf and label the bins today than write a plan for it.
    • Warm and direct. You assume good intent, and you can tell a busy engineer their bench has slipped in a way that feels like help.
    • A systems builder who knows the difference between a system people use and one they work around.
    • Comfortable with hand and power tools, and able to tell a fastener, a connector, and a piece of stock apart.
    • Able to lift 40+ lbs, operate a pallet stacker, and work around robots and machine tools.
    • Willing to pitch in when something lands outside your scope.

      • Nice to haves

      • Experience running a stockroom, tool crib, makerspace, or lab.
      • Hands-on experience with 3D printers, electronics, CNC machines, or sheet metal.
      • Shipping, receiving, and freight experience; pallet jack or forklift certification.
      • Purchasing experience (McMaster-Carr, Digi-Key, and similar).
      • Familiarity with inventory or MES software; ION is a plus.
      • Experience with equipment teardown, salvage, or reselling surplus.
      • A track record of building your own organization solutions.

Manage the Firm's assets, input and manage service requests, and monitor and manage floor plans.

title: Biorepository Technician I
description:
Position Summary:

The Biorepository Technician I will assist in shipment & receipt, the retrieval and preservation of biological samples that arrive daily or are stored in the repository.

Essential functions of the job include but are not limited to:

Monitoring of freezers:

  • Respond to freezer alarms in accordance with standard operating procedures
  • Monitor freezers, refrigerator and room temperatures as assigned by Manager

Receive biological samples:

  • Unpack specimens and record all pertinent information in Incoming Shipment Batch and incoming folder
  • Create a folder to house all associated paperwork
  • Store at appropriate temperature following guidelines set by procedures
  • Distribute confirmation of shipment receipt form if required by project

Receive supplies into inventory:

  • Verify shipment contents against packing list
  • Quarantine Raw Materials for release by QA department

Inventory of Frozen Biological Samples:

  • Check information on sample vial against information provided by the study site
  • Scan samples into data management system, BSI
  • Correct paperwork where necessary and inform supervisor/manager of any discrepancies by generating a discrepancy report
  • Assist in the inventory of returned specimens
  • Aliquot frozen specimens utilizing aseptic technique

Retrieve Frozen Samples from Inventory and Ship:

  • Pull samples according to requisition, SOP, and instructions
  • Perform quality control verification of outgoing samples
  • Update Outgoing Batch Record
  • Contact receiving labs prior to shipment to confirm shipping address and ensure contact will be available to receive specimens
  • Ship samples (dangerous and non-dangerous goods) by Commercial or local courier
  • Complete all paperwork (link-up forms, aliquot forms, return forms or BSI data collection sheets and any other forms which may be necessary)

Miscellaneous:

  • Label vials and shipping boxes
  • Perform dry shipper QC
  • Keep current on IATA Shipping Regulations and maintain certification and standards
  • Carry out other duties/projects as assigned

Qualifications:

Minimum Required:

  • High School Diploma and 2 years’ of relevant working experience or
  • Bachelor’s Degree (Biology, Chemistry, Life Sciences or other related discipline) and 0-2 years of relevant working experience

Other Required:

  • Requires good attention to detail, excellent documentation skills and must work well in a group environment
  • Familiarity with excel and basic functions with the program
  • Must be a flexible agile team player who can change activities and directions quickly and respond to a variety of assignment and changing business needs
  • Ability to lift and carry between 31-50 lbs.; Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. overhead with assistance; frequently required to sit, stand and walk for prolonged periods; occasionally required to squat, bend, stoop, push, kneel, reach and perform tasks with repetitive motion; Will be exposed to a cold freezer environment (Freezer temperatures range between -20ºC -196ºC)
  • Must be able to read, write, speak fluently and comprehend the English language

Preferred:

  • 1 year of relevant lab experience
  • Possess basic laboratory skills
  • Trained in aseptic technique

title: Term Trader II-III
description:
PURPOSE: The Term Trader III manages the day-ahead and forward power positions of AEPCO's members across both centralized ISO/RTO markets and bilateral, over-the-counter physical markets in the Western Interconnection (WECC). This role is responsible for optimizing generation and load positions in term ISO/RTO markets, as well as negotiating and executing bilateral purchase/sale transactions directly with counterparties, arranging and confirming transmission service across western paths, and tagging and scheduling physical delivery across WECC balancing authorities.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, or related field.
  • Three to five years of prior experience in real-time or short-term power trading, scheduling, or transmission operations, spanning ISO/RTO markets and/or WECC bilateral markets.
  • Strong understanding of wholesale electricity market structures, forward curve dynamics, generation economics, LMPs, congestion, and ancillary services in ISO/RTO and WECC bilateral markets.
  • Hands-on, working knowledge of the NERC e-Tag system (creating, approving, adjusting, and curtailing tags) and the physical/contract path tagging process across WECC balancing authorities.
  • Practical experience with OASIS for reserving, confirming, and managing transmission service.
  • Strong understanding of standard bilateral trading terms (EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement, WSPP Agreement).
  • Proficiency with trading and scheduling systems (e.g. MCG, PowerOptix), e-Tag authoring tools, and market data platforms (e.g. OMS, CROW, CIDI).
  • Strong Excel skills; comfortable working with large datasets.
  • Ability to make quick, well-reasoned decisions under time pressure and market volatility.
  • Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work cross-functionally with counterparties, schedulers, transmission system operators, and balancing authorities.
  • Current AEPCO Trading Qualification Card or ability to pass within 6 months.
  • Maintain an active NERC Operator certification is preferred, e.g. Balancing and Interchange (BI) or Reliability Coordinator (RC).
  • Ability to train other Term Traders.
  • Any equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience can be substituted for requirements listed above.

REQUIRED FUNCTIONS:

  • Monitor and manage day-ahead and forward power positions across assigned ISO/RTO markets (e.g., CAISO, CAISO WEIM, SPP RTOE, SPP Markets+) in compliance with market tariffs, protocols, and business practice manuals.
  • Negotiate and execute physical power trades bilaterally with counterparties consistent with standard EEI/WSPP master agreement terms at western hubs and delivery points (e.g. Palo Verde, Four Corners, Mead, NP15/SP15 nodes) to optimize portfolio positions and manage imbalances.
  • Continuously assess load forecasts, generation output, energy limitations (e.g. hydro allocations, emission limits, battery state-of-charge), transmission path/node congestion, and weather patterns (including snowpack and runoff) to inform trading and scheduling decisions across both market structures.
  • Identify and capitalize on arbitrage opportunities between ISO/RTO nodes and western bilateral hubs/paths, and across time periods.
  • Prepare, submit, and manage NERC e-Tags across WECC balancing authority areas; ensure tags are approved by all relevant BAs and transmission providers ahead of flow.
  • Arrange, reserve, and manage transmission service via OASIS on key western paths, including point-to-point and network transmission requests, curtailment tracking, and redirects.
  • Coordinate with generation asset operators, counterparty schedulers, and transmission teams to ensure accurate and timely fuel nominations, schedules, and e-Tags.
  • Accurately input transaction and tag data into applicable software; investigate and resolve discrepancies to reconcile trade data and e-Tag records in coordination with middle office and settlements.
  • Manage risk exposure within established position and credit limits-escalating issues or violations as appropriate-and collaborate with risk management, credit, and compliance teams to ensure adherence to trading policies, master agreement terms, and regulatory requirements.
  • Assist in training junior traders.
  • Actively promote and maintain a team environment.

title: Part-time Clinic Associate
description:

Position Summary:

As a Part-time Clinic Associate at the Seattle Humane Veterinary Clinic, you will ensure pristine cleanliness, efficient stocking, and meticulous organization. Working in a veterinary hospital, the Clinic Associate will be exposed to sick and injured animals and animals undergoing surgery, medical care, and euthanasia. This is an entry level position; while the focus of this position is not on direct animal handling and care, training in these areas will be provided. The Clinic Associate supports the mission, goals, and values of Seattle Humane.

KEY OR ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Responsible for performing routine janitorial services in the Seattle Humane Veterinary Clinic including sweeping, mopping, dusting, restocking soap, paper towels, and hand sanitizers, taking out trash, recycling and compost from clinic locations.
  • Responsible for clinic & surgery cleaning, stocking, organization, pack wrapping, instrument sterilization and laundry.
  • Responsible for thoroughly cleaning and disinfecting animal kennels and common areas.
  • Animal husbandry duties, which include cleaning, feeding, and watering all animals in the veterinary clinic to maintain high standards of veterinary care.
  • Fills medications as prescribed by a veterinarian.
  • Facilitate efficient supply management by handling deliveries, unpacking goods, and organizing them in designated storage areas, ensuring smooth operations for the entire team.
  • Assists with inventory counts or procedures pertaining to the department.
  • Performs work safely and supports a safety culture in the work environment.
  • Cultivate strong relationships with clinic volunteers, leveraging teamwork to deliver exceptional care experiences and uphold Seattle Humane's mission.



Secondary Functions:

  • Animal movement and restraint, particularly related to surgery patients.
  • Other duties as assigned



SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY:
May be called upon to assist/instruct volunteers assigned to the department.

COMMUNICATION/INTERPERSONAL CONTACT:

  • Commits to valuing diversity and contributes to an inclusive working environment that is sensitive to other opinions, culture, and perspectives.
  • Daily verbal and written communication with Veterinary Services and Foster Teams through maintenance schedule, meetings, email, meetings and in person
  • Regular internal contact with other departments

COMPLEXITY:

The Clinic Associate works daily on a diverse set of tasks although there is recurring work during weekly cleaning and maintenance duties. Must be able to coordinate several tasks within a day and remain on schedule with work assignments or projects.

KNOWLEDGE/EXPERIENCE/EDUCATION OR TRAINING:

  • Ability to obtain Veterinary Medication Clerk License (can be obtained on the job)
  • Requires a basic knowledge of animal behavior
  • Must be able to work independently
  • Must have good communication skills
  • Should be able to identify personal limitations and be willing to ask for help
  • Must have a basic knowledge of Microsoft Office applications like Excel, Outlook, and Word or willingness to learn
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks at once

LICENSES/CERTIFICATIONS REQUIRED:

  • None.

PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS:

Must be able to routinely lift and carry up to 50 pounds with or without accommodation. Position requires frequent standing, bending, kneeling, pushing, pulling and grasping of objects. Frequently uses eyesight to and hand dexterity to manipulate tools and equipment. Must be able to work efficiently under stressful conditions. Must be able to recognize problems and analyze possible solutions. Attention to detail is important. Must exhibit initiative and motivation in performing all duties. Should be able to work independently or as part of a team.



WORKING CONDITIONS:

General office environment: Primarily indoor working conditions in a clinic setting for nine to twelve hours per day. Some work may be done in kennels or outdoors.

Equipment Use: Exposures to potential hazards include waste anesthetic gases, radiation, cleaning chemicals and disinfectants, formalin, needles, scalpel blades and other sharp hazards, animal bites and scratches, zoonotic diseases, animal hair, dander and wastes, pharmaceutical and biological agents, euthanasia solution, eye hazards, steam (from autoclave), wet floors, potential electrical hazards, constant noise (vacuum, fan, barking) and interruptions, back strain, exposure to cold or other hazards with walk-in freezer.

Work Hours: Part-time, non-exempt, hourly position. Scheduled for 24 hours per week; the schedule is flexible but ideally there would be some availability for weekend work.

The position works in an onsite capacity, located in the Bellevue, WA office.

Equal Opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, Seattle Humane is committed to providing employment opportunities to all qualified applicants and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability status or any other basis prohibited by applicable law.



SEATTLE HUMANE CORE VALUES:

Candidate should be committed to Seattle Humane’s Core Values:

Collaboration

Compassion

Accessibility

Respect

Adaptability


WHO WE ARE:

Seattle Humane is more than a shelter; we’re a community resource center. We're meeting the increasing need for pet owner support services so that families don't have to choose between an overdue bill and a beloved family member. We're training the next generation of veterinarians in our state-of-the-art medical center. We're building a community of animal advocates through our volunteer and youth education programs. The impact of Seattle Humane is life-changing, for the animals in our care and the people who love them. Our top priority is to connect animals in need of rescue with the people who will love them. Through our outreach, advocacy and services, we strive to ensure that animal companionship is accessible to all.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Bioinformatics
description:
Job Description

About Variantyx

Join our rapidly growing, engineering-driven organization and help build the software that powers the future of whole genome diagnostics. Backed by leading life sciences investors, we have achieved industry-leading diagnostic yield and unit economics through a fully vertically integrated pipeline that spans from sample to report. At the core of our success is a proprietary clinical platform that uniquely enables our workflows, allowing us to solve complex biological data challenges at scale. With a strong global presence across our internal teams and external partnerships, we offer the stability of a well-funded industry leader combined with the agility of a high-growth tech company.


About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Senior Software Engineer to lead the architectural evolution of our core germline clinical bioinformatics pipeline.


Our production pipeline is a large-scale, high-throughput system written primarily in Python. We continue to push the frontier of diagnostic capabilities while also heavily scaling our operations. As part of a small team, you will be expected to take ownership of your work, and to provide clean, well-tested, well-documented, optimized code.


This is not a research position; it is a production engineering role. You will not just be running tools; you will be designing and implementing new variant detection modules, supporting and refactoring legacy logic, and identifying key areas for optimization. In addition to translating business requirements into precise technical specifications and implementing them, you will be expected to understand how your code supports our business workflows and how your code affects other teams. Working in a highly-regulated clinical environment means enforcing strict software quality standards to ensure our clinical results are accurate and reproducible, every single time.


What You Will Do

  • Performance Engineering: Identify bottlenecks and opportunities for optimization in our core primary, secondary, and tertiary bioinformatics pipelines.
  • Increase Automation: You will help scale sample throughput by automating business processes, from tasks in the development lifecycle to tasks in the production workflow.
  • Feature Development: You will design, develop, validate, and deploy cutting-edge algorithms for clinical-grade variant detection, making use of our high-performance CPU and GPU compute cluster.


Required Qualifications

Master's in Computer Science, Mathematics, Computational Biology, or similar. 3+ years of industry experience.


  • Production Software Engineering: You are experienced developing production-grade software. You understand the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) deeply. You are experienced with pytest, mocking strategies, and writing modular, testable code.
  • Python Mastery: You are an expert in Python internals, packaging, and design patterns. You know how to untangle complex dependencies and write clean, Pythonic code.
  • Linux/Bash Expert: You live in the terminal. You are comfortable debugging complex interactions in a Linux environment and writing robust shell scripts.
  • Bioinformatics Expertise: Production experience, and significant experience with standard file formats (FASTQ / BAM / CRAM / VCF) and variant calling algorithms and common tools. Experience with short- and long-read sequencing platforms.
  • Strong Architecture Sense: You have experience designing and implementing efficient new processes in a complex environment.


Preferred Qualifications

PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Computational Biology, or similar. 5+ years of industry experience.


  • Typescript Experience: Experience writing Typescript, to interface with our MongoDB data layer and execute workflows.
  • Rust Experience: Experience writing Rust, particularly for Python extensions (Maturin/PyO3). C++ experience is also acceptable if you are willing to learn Rust.
  • Database Design: Experience with MongoDB and Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS). Experience designing normalized schemas and performing data migrations.


Compensation and Benefits

  • Employee Stock Options Plan (ESOP)
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, and Disability insurance
  • 401k Retirement Savings Plan

title: Operations Resident
description:
Job Title: Operations Resident

Group/Team: Operations

Reports to: Operations Mentor

Location: Remote

Employment Type: Part-time, 20-week contract, hourly

Time Period: Jan. 25–Jun. 11, 2027

WHO WE ARE

We're all creatives here, even if your title doesn't say so.

MAS is an award-winning experiential agency driven by people who care deeply about the work and the impact it creates. We design immersive environments, live moments, and digitally integrated experiences that challenge brands to move beyond the expected.

At MAS we don't settle for anything less than more.

We'd rather hear the idea that scares us than the one that plays it safe, so bring your boldest self, we’re built for it. We're not for everyone. But we're everything for our people.

MAS is a member of the Opus Group, a collective of agencies including Verve and Opus Agency who together create experiences that create action for the world's most influential brands. That gives us shared services across IT, HR, Finance, and Legal, and a network of teams we lean on for best practices and global resources.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

The MAS Residency program is a 20-week tasting of our MAS special sauce — who we are, what we do, and how we do it. It's a deep dive into the experiential marketing industry, where fresh minds can immerse themselves in our world (and our clients’). During this time, residents will have the opportunity to hone and grow their skills, while also uncovering new interests and opportunities along the way. Ultimately this is a unique chance to collaborate closely with leading experts in the field, forge invaluable professional connections, actively contribute to the agency’s perspective, and depart with substantial portfolio work.

We’re not looking for coffee runners, we’re looking for cultural collaborators! We're looking for standout candidates ready to go above and beyond what is asked for. We want relentless learners, envelope-pushers, and creatives who are immune to ordinary thinking. You’re not just here to sit in and watch how the magic happens; you’re here to roll up your sleeves and help shape the future for the world’s most influential brands.

Now you might be thinking, this all sounds great, but what does Operations look like at MAS? Good question! We are looking for an exceptionally organized, detail-oriented person eager to learn about the systems and processes that keep a fast-moving experiential agency running. As an Operations Resident, you will support the team across onboarding, freelancer contracting, vendor research, documentation, internal initiatives, and process improvement while gaining hands-on exposure to the work that keeps people, projects, and information moving.

Feeling it? Awesome, we’d love to have you!

YOU SHOULD HAVE

  • A drive to soak up industry knowledge, ask questions, and be proactive in every task you take on.

  • An interest in business administration, live events, and the operational work that supports agency teams.

  • High attention to detail and a natural instinct for keeping information organized.

  • Comfort learning and navigating new digital tools and platforms.

  • Familiarity with Google Workspace (including Slides, Sheets, Docs, and Drive).

  • Clear and confident written and verbal skills, across drafting emails, participating in video calls, messaging the team, and more.

  • Solid time-management and basic project-management abilities to help keep fast-moving projects on track.

  • Strong research skills and the ability to organize information into clear, useful takeaways.

  • A collaborative attitude amid shifting timelines and priorities.

  • Professionalism and discretion when working with sensitive employee, freelancer, vendor, or business information.

  • Note: you will need access to a personal laptop for the duration of the 20-week program.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Participate in a special capstone project with fellow residents that will result in a one-of-a-kind portfolio piece.

  • Work closely with your Operations mentor to tackle project tasks and learn how Operations supports MAS employees, freelancers, production teams, and agency-wide initiatives.

  • Assist with new-hire onboarding by helping schedule sessions, organize training materials, and track required steps.

  • Support the administrative side of freelancer contracting by helping gather information, maintain documentation, update trackers, and learn how Salesforce is used throughout the process.

  • Assist with freelancer credit-card assignments and related administrative support.

  • Research potential vendors and organize findings to support future production and agency needs.

  • Help maintain clear documentation for vendor management, onboarding, contracting, and other Operations processes.

  • Support process-improvement work by gathering information, organizing team feedback, documenting next steps, and helping identify operational gaps.

  • Assist with internal projects that support team culture, including agency swag, social initiatives, and the annual company offsite.

  • Help organize training resources and process documentation used by full-time employees and freelancers.

  • Keep the team inspired by sharing useful tools, emerging platforms, and ideas that could improve how work gets done.

  • Act as an engaged team member who contributes to MAS’s culture, perspective, and growth.

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT IN RETURN

  • Temporary contract position with potential for extension or conversion.

  • A collaborative, inclusive, and enthusiastic team

HOW WE’LL TAKE CARE OF YOU

Our job titles may span more than one career level. The starting pay for this role is $22.00 per hour. Our pay ranges are based on third-party national average market compensation analysis. The actual pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs, and market demands. The pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

CREATIVE SUBMISSION

*SUBMIT A CREATIVE PRESENTATION ABOUT YOURSELF*

We want to get to know you! In place of a coverletter, this creative presentation is an opportunity to share how you work, projects you’re proud of, what you’re passionate about, and why MAS. Choose 1 of the MAS values, (outlined below), and share an experience that shaped you. Don’t be shy; use this presentation as an opportunity to highlight your unique personality and perspective. TL;DR BE YOU. We’re here for it.


MAS Values:

  • KEEP GOOD COMPANY - It’s about showing up in all the right ways — the friend, the devil’s advocate, the hype squad — and keeping it a damn good time through it all.

  • HAVE SOME GUTS - This is about being bold with purpose — pushing the envelope to inspire new ideas, surprise our audiences, and go beyond the expected.

  • HOLD NOTHING BACK - It’s about never settling for anything less than more — or whatever you define as the best. Day to day, it’s showing up with fiery passion, big dreams (because why the hell not), and the determination to take your shot and challenge what’s comfortable.

  • GET EMOTIONAL - This is about being madly devoted to giving a shit — they seriously can’t help the fact that they’re so passionate.

  • STAY HUNGRY - This is about always exploring, tinkering, expanding skill sets, soaking up inspiration, and asking those what if questions.

Submissions should be submitted as a PDF, but can consist of:

  • An Image/collage or mood board

  • A Word Doc (1 page max)

  • A Deck (5 slides max)

  • A Video or Audio recording (1 minute max - embedded link)

Opportunity to Present:

There will be an opportunity to present for no more than 5 minutes during the 2nd round interviews.

SUBMISSION PROCESS

  1. Create your Presentation

  2. Submit your Resume, Presentation, and other relevant Candidate Info via this Job Posting

APPLICATION DEADLINE

Applications and presentations will be accepted till filled.

NOT SURE IF YOU SHOULD APPLY?

Studies show that those identifying as under-represented individuals might have talked themselves out of applying at this point. Don’t worry about checking every single box. At MAS, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic team – so if you’re excited about this role, but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every single qualification in this job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may just be the right candidate for this role or we may have other roles that better align with your skillset.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Individuals will be required to sit for the majority of the day and may be required to stand as needed. May require ability to ambulate primarily on a level surface for periodic periods throughout the day. Individuals may be required to travel via airplane, train, taxi, car and/or other means of transportation, as needed.

The job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice.

OTHER DUTIES AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT

The above noted job description is not intended to describe, in detail, the multitude of tasks that may be assigned but rather to give the employee/ candidate a general sense of the responsibilities and expectations of the position. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice. This does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an "at will" relationship. We are seeking a Senior HRIS Analyst to own and evolve our Workday platform. This role primarily focuses on payroll administration, and payroll administration experience is required. You'll also bring strong Core HCM expertise and support other Workday functional areas, including Time and Absence and Advanced Compensation. This role is responsible for designing, configuring, and optimizing scalable payroll and people systems that enable business growth and operational efficiency. You will act as a strategic partner to People, Finance, Total Rewards, and Payroll teams—translating business needs into system solutions while ensuring payroll accuracy, data integrity, and streamlined processes across the employee lifecycle.

We are in the midst of an exciting Intelligent Work Systems transformation, evolving from manual operations to designing AI-enabled, cross-system workflows that scale across the enterprise. We’re looking for someone with a strong Workday payroll foundation and an inventor mindset to help build what’s next.

The Mountain View base salary range for this full-time position is $184,000-$226,000, plus equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. If based in or near Mountain View, CA, the role requires in-office work 2 days a week, though we are open to remote candidates in PT or CT time zones.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Payroll & Workday Configuration Ownership

  • Administer Workday Payroll configuration end-to-end, including pay groups, earnings, deductions, and payroll-impacting business processes
  • Serve as the primary systems point of contact for Payroll Operations, ensuring accurate, on-time pay processing
  • Own configuration and ongoing optimization of Workday Payroll and also other areas in Core HCM, including security frameworks as assigned
  • Support configuration and troubleshooting across other Workday functional areas, including Time and Absence
  • Design and maintain business processes, workflows, and system controls across the employee lifecycle
  • Lead system enhancements, releases, and feature adoption in areas assigned

System Strategy & Optimization

  • Ensure Workday is not operated in isolation but as part of a broader enterprise ecosystem; design solutions that support end-to-end business processes across systems, including access governance, compliance, and cross-functional workflow orchestration
  • Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, and automate People processes through Workday and integrated systems
  • Drive scalable solutions that reduce manual effort and improve data accuracy
  • Contribute to the Workday roadmap by defining and prioritizing enhancements based on business impact, scalability, and system health
  • Establish and maintain system governance and best practices
  • Partner with People Operations and external Workday support to manage escalations, prioritize issues, and drive systemic resolution of recurring problems
  • Ensure data consistency and integrity across Workday and downstream financial systems, including reconciliation of headcount, compensation, and organizational structures used in financial reporting and planning.
  • Develop and maintain system documentation (business processes, decision logic, architecture diagrams); leverage AI tools to accelerate documentation, identify logic gaps, and propose enhancements
  • Troubleshoot system issues, root-cause errors, and implement scalable fixes

Reporting & Insights

  • Build and maintain advanced Workday reports, dashboards, and calculated fields
  • Partner with stakeholders to deliver actionable insights across People and Finance
  • Ensure consistency and integrity of workforce data

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with People Ops, Accounting, Payroll, Total Rewards, Finance, and IT to translate business requirements into system solutions
  • Act as a subject matter expert on Workday capabilities and limitations
  • Act as a key partner to Finance in supporting workforce planning, budgeting, and actuals reporting by ensuring accurate and timely workforce data
  • Support testing strategy (UAT) and ensure high-quality system deployments
  • Leverage AI and structured methodologies to define test strategies, generate test cases, support design reviews, and proactively identify logic gaps or architectural improvements prior to deployment

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 3+ years of hands-on Workday Payroll configuration and administration experience, required
  • 5+ years of HRIS experience with deep Workday expertise
  • Strong configuration experience in Workday Payroll and Core HCM
  • Experience with Workday configuration including Business Process Framework, Security, and Advanced Reporting (Calculated Fields)
  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with stakeholders in People, Accounting, Payroll, Finance, and IT
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Experience creating structured documentation and leveraging AI tools to enhance system design, testing, and analysis
  • Advanced analytical and technical skills for translating and analyzing business needs into requirements, driving implementations, and delivering effective, value-adding solutions
  • Exceptional technical aptitude and strong desire for learning new technologies and solution architectures
  • Experience with Workday’s tools below is a plus:
    • Advanced Compensation
    • Time and Absence
    • Talent/Performance modules
    • Workday Extend
  • Experience in global and matrixed organizations is a plus
  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Information Systems, or equivalent is a plus
  • Experience designing workflows across different areas in the employment lifecycle (recruiting, onboarding, career development, off-boarding) is a plus

Bend, Oregon 97703

Position Title: EDUCATIONAL ASSISTANT – INCLUSION

Department: Special Programs

Reports To: Assigned Teacher and Site Administrator

JOB DEFINITION:

Under direct supervision, the Educational Assistant – Inclusion, provides supported education services in classrooms, resource centers, or other school-related areas. The Educational Assistant is directly involved in the instructional program for assigned students and their identified special needs. The responsibilities include in and out of class supervision of students; small group and one on one instruction of students; and general assistance to the teacher. The employee works independently after becoming familiar with the instructional needs of the special needs students and seeks clarification from the teacher for new or unusual situations. The employee works on a daily basis with disabled students who require special attention to meet their unique needs. The employee works under the supervision of a special education teacher and/or administrator.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

  • Assists with implementing individualized education plan (IEP).
  • Assists special education teaching staff responsible for preparation, implementation, and evaluation of individual and group instructional programs.
  • Assists in communicating with teachers and parents on students’ progress.
  • Assists with record keeping to monitor students’ daily and monthly data on progress.
  • Assists students’ in their understanding of instructional concepts by reemphasizing the basic elements of teacher directed activities.
  • Provides students with additional practice on identified skill areas.
  • Assists with the correction of student work as assigned by the classroom teacher.
  • Prepares instructional materials and operates instructional equipment.
  • Supervises students during recess, lunch periods, and before / after school by keeping a calm and disciplined atmosphere on the playground, in the cafeteria, library, hallways, and bus lines.
  • Assists in monitoring the daily school routines of a small group and / or individual low functioning student.
  • Participates in the various vocational / recreational activities developed for ILSC / FLSC students.
  • Assists the special education teaching staff in maintaining the practical life skills such as dressing, toileting and feeding students with mildly to profoundly disabling conditions in the District’s ILSC / FLSC program.
  • Follows the assigned daily schedule.
  • Fulfills other related duties as assigned.
  • Fulfills performance standards identified in the evaluation process as required by the position.
  • Fulfills working conditions and physical effort listed below.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Work is performed primarily indoors in classroom or specialized instructional settings, with occasional outdoor supervision. The position requires standing, walking, bending, kneeling, and assisting students with mobility or personal care needs. The role may involve lifting or supporting students or equipment consistent with assigned duties.

The employee may be exposed to escalated student behaviors and may encounter bodily fluids while providing direct support. Work follows the assigned school schedule and may include participation in school activities.

The role requires attentiveness, patience, consistent implementation of intervention strategies, and collaboration with licensed staff to support student learning and safety. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

Knowledge:

  • Teaching methods and procedures.
  • Filing and record keeping systems.
  • Computers, audio-visual equipment and office machines, and their operation.
  • Instructional materials and their uses.
  • Basic provisions of PL-142, due process procedures, and the IEPs for students identified as disabled.
  • Student behavior and methods to assure proper conduct.
  • Safety practices.

Skills & Abilities:

Possess the physical ability to regularly attend work and fulfill the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Read, understand and carry out oral and written instructions.
  • Learn the operation of telephones, computers, and other equipment used in the work, as required by the position.
  • Accurately transfer, record and convey information, and materials as required by the position.
  • Train and supervise student helpers.
  • Communicate clearly and appropriately in speech and in writing in accordance with educational standards.
  • Promote the success of special education programs and the students served by these programs.
  • Maintain patient, positive, persistent attitude and a warm, accepting personality toward persons with disabilities.
  • Ability to learn how to deal with bodily fluid spills.
  • Adhere to the district requirements for a drug-free workplace.
  • Abide by confidentiality requirements.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

At least two years of related college education, an AA degree, or meet the Highly Qualified requirements by passing the Paraprofessional Assessment Exam with a score of 455 or higher

The position requires general knowledge of technical procedures. Knowledge of School District practices or policies is necessary. Job proficiency can be acquired in twelve to twenty-four months.

CERTIFICATION AND LICENSING:

NCLB (No Child Left Behind) Paraprofessional qualifications for positions at sites that are designated as Title I School- wide programs.

Expectations of Professional Conduct:

Employees of Bend-La Pine Schools are expected to adhere to all Bend-La Pine Schools policies and regulations, ensuring compliance with established procedures and expectations. They are to prioritize the well-being of students, aligning their conduct with the core values of public education and the mission, vision, and goals of Bend-La Pine Schools. This entails maintaining consistent and punctual attendance while adhering to site and/or district protocols for reporting absences.

Professionalism extends to personal presentation, with employees expected to maintain attire and grooming appropriate to their roles. While carrying out everyday tasks independently, it's essential to maintain professionalism in how you communicate, both verbally and nonverbally, with students, parents/guardians, the public, and colleagues. This includes valuing and respecting cultural and background differences. Employees of Bend-La Pine Schools are entrusted with fostering a respectful working and learning environment, upholding confidentiality regarding student, staff, and district information at all times.

The statements herein reflect the general nature and level of work expected in this position and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or qualifications.

Employees may be assigned additional duties as needed to support district operations, provide coverage, and ensure the effective functioning of the organization. This may include location changes to the assignment in order to address developing district needs.

Please Provide:

Resume

Evidence of Highly Qualified status

Note: The system will not take uploads from current employees, so please email supporting documents to hr-recruitment@bend.k12.or.us

title: Enterprise Project Manager
description:
About Staffbase

We inspire people to achieve great things together. Our mission is to help organizations unlock the power of inspirational communication with the first AI-native Employee Experience Platform. Our industry-leading and award-winning agentic AI communications channels - intranet, employee app and email solutions - create engaging experiences that connect and empower employees.

Headquartered in Chemnitz, Germany and New York City, with offices in Berlin, London, Sydney, Tokyo, Prague, and Minneapolis–St. Paul, our diverse team of 550+ employees supports 1,500+ customers—reaching over 14 million employees—in transforming their employee experience.
We are proud to be a Unicorn company—privately valued at over $1 billion—demonstrating strong growth, innovation, and lasting impact in our industry. Together, we’re shaping the future of workplace communication.

Staffbase is the employee communications platform that connects the world's largest workforces, from the corner office to the frontline. Our Professional Services team leads the most complex, highest-stakes launches. We run custom builds, multi-system integrations, and enterprise rollouts that our biggest customers stake their internal communications strategy on.

This is the team that turns an ambitious, one-of-a-kind vision into a platform that is live, adopted, and loved. We are hiring an Enterprise Project Manager to lead these bespoke implementations and custom solution engagements for our Fortune 100 customers.

What you’ll lead

No two engagements look the same, and that is the point. In the last twelve months alone, this team has:

  • Replatformed how 7-Eleven reaches both its corporate teams and its franchise stores, wiring up Workday and secure store data feeds, retiring legacy tooling, and driving a phased go-live against hard deadlines across IT, comms, and operations
  • Engineered a custom shift-swap experience for Chipotle, built directly into their mobile app on top of their workforce-management system, from use-case and edge-case definition through UAT and acceptance
  • Partnered on Ford's migration off a legacy platform and onto Staffbase, co-delivered with an implementation partner under a single, unified project plan and clear scope governance
  • Launched a bilingual, security-first rollout with Bell Canada, navigating translation quality, data privacy and anonymization, and enterprise InfoSec and compliance review
  • Facilitated hands-on Foundations and content-strategy workshops with Waste Management, helping a largely deskless workforce reimagine how information reaches the field

A week in this role might include

  • Owning the end-to-end plan for a custom engagement, from scoping statement through design, build, testing, and launch, so the customer only ever experiences one clear timeline
  • Running the room: aligning customer IT, communications, and operations stakeholders alongside our solution engineers, integration specialists, and Customer Success leads
  • Holding the line on scope with warmth and clarity, so custom work stays deliverable and change requests are surfaced early, not discovered late
  • Coordinating implementation partners and internal experts so hand-offs are seamless and nothing falls through the cracks
  • Turning technical complexity (integrations, data models, security reviews, migrations) into plain-language decisions a customer executive can make with confidence

What you'll bring

  • 8+ years of project or program management experience, leading complex, enterprise software implementations or custom solution engagements, ideally for Fortune 100 or similarly sophisticated customers
  • Proven ability to facilitate discussions with multiple customer stakeholders with competing priorities, sustaining constructive dialogue and long-term relationship integrity
  • Fluency in translating between technical teams and business owners, and comfort around integrations, data, security, and migration conversations
  • Demonstrated track record running formal governance on complex, multi-stakeholder technical programs, ideally at consultancy or enterprise-software scale
  • Comfortable owning a hard conversations both internally and with the customer when scope and timeline collide, not just reporting status
  • Proven ability to build and manage detailed project plans, budgets, and resource allocation across multiple concurrent enterprise engagements
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience delivering executive-ready readouts, steering committee updates, and status reporting
  • Working knowledge of PM tooling and delivery frameworks (e.g., Jira, Smartsheet, MS Project, Agile/Scrum ceremonies) to keep distributed teams aligned
  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with Sales, Solutions Engineering, and Customer Success to ensure seamless handoffs from implementation to steady-state support
  • A bias toward ownership: you plan the work, you drive the work, and you own the outcome
  • Calm under pressure, genuine care for the customer, and the judgment to know when to escalate and when to solve

Why this role

Because the work is real, visible, and hard in the best way. You will lead launches that reach hundreds of thousands of employees at some of the most recognizable brands in the world. You will build things that have never been built on our platform before. And you will do it alongside a team that genuinely likes each other and takes pride in getting the hard ones right.

If you love a hard problem, a room full of stakeholders, and the moment it all goes live, this is your kind of work.

What you'll get

  • Competitive Compensation - we offer attractive salary packages including LTIP (unit-based Long Term Incentive Plan)
  • Flexibility - we offer flexible working time models and the option of hybrid work, and support this with a yearly flex work allowance of $1608
  • Recharge - with 31 vacation days annually (incl. one floating holiday), plus pro rata fully paid Fridays off during August
  • Support - we’re offering a 401(k) plan with company match and health plans, including dental & vision as well as competitive Paid Parental Leave to support new parents
  • Volunteer Day - you’ll get one day off per year for supporting a social project
