Digital Health Center of Excellence (DHCoE), Office of Strategic Partnerships and Technology Innovation (OST), Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH), FDA

Position Summary

The Healthcare AI Evaluation and Risk Assessment Specialist provides scientific, technical, and regulatory expertise supporting FDA's oversight of AI-enabled medical devices. The incumbent serves as a subject matter expert in the evaluation of emerging healthcare AI technologies, including generative AI, large language models (LLMs), foundation models, multimodal AI systems, and agentic AI, and their application in medical devices across clinical specialties. The position focuses on evaluating safety, effectiveness, performance, reliability, risk management, and evidence supporting AI-enabled medical devices and contributing to regulatory science, policy development, and review best practices. [fda.gov], [fda.gov]

Major Duties and Responsibilities

  • Review premarket submissions, IDE applications, and other regulatory submissions involving AI-enabled medical devices
  • Evaluate AI model performance, validation strategies, benchmarking methodologies, and supporting evidence for safety and effectiveness
  • Assess AI risk assessment and risk management approaches, including model failure modes, hallucinations, bias, automation bias, cybersecurity risks, human factors, post-market monitoring, and lifecycle management
  • Evaluate model testing approaches, including benchmarking, robustness testing, subgroup analyses, uncertainty quantification, stress testing, and adversarial testing (red teaming)
  • Identify scientific limitations of proposed evaluation designs, datasets, scoring methodologies, and validation approaches
  • Assess evidence from clinical studies, reader studies, simulation-based evaluations, real-world evidence, and external validation studies
  • Provide scientific consultation to multidisciplinary review teams on AI evaluation methodologies, evidence generation, transparency, explainability, governance, and performance monitoring
  • Collaborate with FDA staff, other Federal agencies, academic institutions, healthcare organizations, standards development organizations, and industry stakeholders
  • Contribute to the development of regulatory science, policy, guidance documents, review methodologies, and best practices related to healthcare AI and emerging digital health technologies
  • Monitor advances in AI technologies and identify scientific challenges and opportunities relevant to FDA's regulatory mission
  • Prepare technical reports, scientific reviews, briefing materials, presentations, and policy analyses

Minimum Qualifications

  • Master's degree or higher in artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer science, data science, biomedical engineering, health informatics, medicine, public health, or a related field
  • At least seven (7) years of relevant experience in healthcare AI, medical devices, digital health, regulatory science, or related disciplines
  • Demonstrated expertise in AI evaluation, risk assessment, evidence generation, and performance assessment methodologies

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD, MD, DVM, PharmD, or other advanced scientific degree
  • Experience supporting FDA or other Federal healthcare agencies
  • Knowledge of:
    • Generative AI and LLMs
    • Foundation and multimodal models
    • Software as a Medical Device (SaMD)
    • Medical device regulatory pathways (510(k), De Novo, PMA, IDE)
    • AI governance and Good Machine Learning Practice (GMLP)
    • Medical device cybersecurity and real-world evidence

title: Emergency Management Specialist - Training, Exercise, and Education
description:
The Emergency Management Specialist (Training, Exercise, & Education Coordinator) is responsible for the development, coordination, delivery, and evaluation of the statewide emergency management training program. The position ensures that training, all-hazards qualifications, and credentialing activities support statewide preparedness priorities. This position coordinates across federal, state, tribal, and local partners to increase the readiness of personnel across all phases of emergency management.

This position falls within the emergency management career ladder which establishes criteria for initial pay and pay increases, based on experience in all aspects of the profession.

Responsibilities\:

  • Develop and maintain the annual training strategy, calendar, and implementation plan aligned with the state Integrated Preparedness Plan, THIRA/SPR process, preparedness grants, and identified capability gaps.
  • Conduct training needs assessments and analyze after-action reports, exercise improvement plans, stakeholder feedback, and incident lessons learned.
  • Design, schedule, coordinate, deliver, and evaluate emergency management training across various platforms to include instructor-led, virtual, and hybrid.
  • Maintain positive relationships with key state and federal partners, professional associations, and local/tribal emergency management personnel.
  • Accurately maintain training records, student registration, certificates, course evaluations, instructor records, and statewide training metrics.
  • Develop and maintain state curricula and course materials using adult-learning and instructional-design principles.
  • Administer standards for instructor qualification, instructor endorsement, course approval, and course quality assurance.
  • Support the state exercise program by ensuring training priorities connect to exercises, corrective actions, and operational readiness.
  • Provide technical assistance to local emergency management agencies in the development and management of training and exercise programs.
  • Prepare briefing materials, annual reports, performance measures, and recommendations for agency leadership.
  • Provide support to the State Emergency Coordination Center as needed.

title: Senior Program Manager, AMZL Field Support
description:
Amazon's middle mile network moves at massive scale, and the technology on every tractor and trailer keeps it running. We are looking for a Senior Program Manager to own the reliability and performance of critical fleet technology platforms deployed across our middle mile transportation network, keeping our fleet connected and packages moving. In this role you will manage complex repair programs, vendor performance, and cross-functional partnerships with product engineering teams, OEM partners, and service providers to maximize device uptime and operational readiness across our tractor, trailer, and intermodal fleet.

You will work backward from network needs to diagnose root causes of device failures, implement systematic repair strategies, and drive continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen fleet technology reliability. You will own vendor relationships, establish performance accountability mechanisms, and coordinate device strategy across transportation networks, aligning shared vendor relationships and measurement standards to unlock scale and consistency.

Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end device operations and repair program execution for critical fleet technology platforms across the middle mile tractor, trailer, and intermodal fleet, defining program strategy and driving teams inside and outside the organization to deliver
- Manage third-party vendor relationships and performance — including SLA enforcement, cost efficiency, and repair quality — while partnering with product engineering and OEM teams to diagnose systemic device failures and accelerate resolution
- Analyze device health and failure data to identify root causes, implement preventive maintenance strategies, and build reporting mechanisms that enable proactive issue identification and data-driven decisions
- Coordinate device repair strategy across transportation networks, aligning intake mechanisms, vendor relationships, and measurement standards to capture scale and reduce complexity
- Communicate program status, technical risks, and recommendations clearly to senior leadership through well-structured narratives and regular business reviews

A day in the life
You might start the morning reviewing overnight device health trends and triaging new failure reports with your engineering counterparts. By mid-morning you are on a call with a repair vendor, working through turnaround-time gaps and agreeing on corrective actions. After lunch you pull together data for a leadership review, translating repair metrics into a clear narrative about fleet readiness. Later you join a design review with the product team to weigh in on a hardware change that could reduce a recurring failure mode. Throughout the day you move between strategic planning and hands-on problem solving, keeping multiple programs on track.

About the team
The Middle Mile Fleet Technology team is responsible for keeping Amazon's fleet technology running reliably at scale. We sit at the intersection of hardware engineering, service operations, and vendor management, and our work directly affects delivery performance across the network.

We are a collaborative group that values clear thinking, practical solutions, and a willingness to get into the details. If you enjoy solving complex operational problems and want to see the real-world impact of your work every day, this is a great place to be.

title: Sr. Software Engineer II - Tech Lead - Data Products
description:
Company Summary

Zoro.com is a leading eCommerce platform offering nearly 12 million tools, parts and supplies for our business customers. Launched in 2011, we brought a B2C-like experience to the B2B industry, and continue to be at the forefront of digital innovation at the intersection of technology and distribution. We have rapidly grown to over $1 billion in annual revenue and we’re just getting started!

About the Role

This is the senior technical role on a data product team, in a data organization that is becoming a software-engineering organization and deliberately reinventing how engineering work is performed with AI. You will set the technical direction for what the team builds: APIs, backend services, shared libraries, operational data stores, and data-processing systems; and you will build alongside the engineers doing it. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports. Every data product team at Zoro runs on a three-way partnership: the product manager owns what gets built and in what order, the engineering manager owns the engineering practice and how engineers grow, and you own how it gets built, including the architecture, the interfaces, the sequencing of the work, and the call on whether a design is ready.

You will be measured by what the team ships, not solely by what you ship yourself. The best tech leads spend their time on the decisions that are expensive to reverse and leave the rest to the engineers who will learn from making them. The role sits at the seam between software engineering and data science and asks for real strength in both: you may not be building models yourself, but you need to be credible with the people who do, and able to reason about whether an offline metric will hold up online, what a latency budget means for an inference path, and when a model is the right tool and when a rule would do. We expect Tech Leads to use AI in their own engineering and to shape how their teams use it.

What You Will Do

  • Own the technical direction and architecture of your team's systems, break large problems into work the team can execute, and make the calls that are expensive to reverse.
  • Stay in the code every week, and use AI throughout design, planning, implementation, testing, and review.
  • Partner with your product manager on feasibility, sequencing, and tradeoffs, early enough to change the plan.
  • Partner with the Data Scientists and ML Engineers on your team, from problem framing through production serving, monitoring, and retraining.
  • Design interfaces, service boundaries, schemas, and data contracts that other teams can rely on, and negotiate them with those teams.
  • Lead design reviews and RFC discussions, and own the call on when a design is ready and on cross-cutting technical tradeoffs.
  • Grow the engineers around you through how you review, and partner with your engineering manager on where each one needs stretch or support.
  • Own your team's operational health: on-call quality, observability, and the systems you have in production.

An Excellent Candidate Has

  • Experience as the Tech Lead on a team building production backend services, APIs, internal platforms, or distributed applications.
  • Experience designing APIs, data contracts, and operational databases that other teams consumed.
  • Familiarity with asynchronous processing, queues, event-driven systems, and change-data capture, including idempotency, retries, concurrency, and backward compatibility.
  • Working knowledge of machine learning and data science concepts: feature engineering, evaluation, training and serving skew, drift, and retraining; enough to review a model design and ask the questions that matter, and experience taking a model from notebook to production.
  • Experience making a team faster, through interfaces, tooling, or decomposition of work.
  • Comfort leading engineers who do not report to them, and partnering with a product manager whose priorities they do not set.
  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, containers, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, and observability.
  • Practical opinions about where AI tools are useful, where they are unreliable, and how to improve their output.

How We Work

We value engineers who take ownership, prefer simple systems, treat operations as part of engineering, ask questions when designs are unclear, give thoughtful feedback, and balance speed with reliability.

We expect Tech Leads to make the call when a decision is theirs, to say clearly when it is not, and to disagree well with product and engineering management when the technical reality warrants it.

We also expect engineers to use AI aggressively but not uncritically, and to share what they learn so the whole team improves.

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience: Minimum 7 years building production software, including at least 2 years as the Tech Lead for a team or a significant system.
  • Experience building, shipping, and operating production software, with strong programming skills beyond SQL.
  • Hands on keyboard every week, designing, building, and reviewing, not only directing.
  • Experience leading the design of a system that multiple engineers built on, and owning it through deployment, incident response, and on-call.
  • Strong grounding in both software engineering and machine learning or data science, and the ability to lead a technical discussion in either.
  • A record of raising the team's output, delegating the decisions engineers will learn from, keeping the ones that are expensive to reverse, and deciding plainly when a design is ready.
  • Influence without authority, earning alignment across teams, negotiating interfaces rather than escalating, and explaining a technical decision clearly to engineers, product managers, and leaders.

Total Rewards

Zoro’s total compensation plan includes our Zoro Incentive Plan (ZIP) that is designed to foster and reward our team members for strong performance. Total compensation will be highly competitive.

In addition to competitive compensation, Zoro offers comprehensive benefits and perks including:

  • Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans with coverage starting on day one of employment
  • Maternity support programs, nursing benefits, and up to 14 weeks paid leave for birth parents and up to 4 weeks paid leave for non-birth parents. We also support growing your family through access to adoption assistance program
  • 6 free sessions each year with a licensed therapist and Wellhub portal membership to support your mental and emotional wellbeing
  • At least 18 paid time off days annually for full-time employees and 6 company holidays per year
  • 6% company contribution to a 401K Retirement Savings Plan each pay period, no employee contribution required
  • Tuition reimbursement, student loan refinancing and access to financial counseling, education, and tools
  • Charitable Gift Program - match gift to an eligible educational, cultural, community health, and human service organizations
  • Employee discounts and admission to various civic and cultural institutions around Chicago
  • Zoro office perks including coffee bar, beer on tap, unlimited snacks, access to the onsite gym, and incredible city skyline views

For additional information and details regarding our benefits and our parent company, W. W. Grainger, please click on the link here.

The pay range provided is not a guarantee of compensation. The range listed reflects the expected base pay for this position at the time of posting, based on the role's job grade. Actual compensation may vary depending on factors such as location, relevant experience and individual qualifications.

Our Culture

Zoro was founded in 2011 with a simple idea: make it easy for businesses to get the tools, parts, and supplies they need to keep things running. We've grown by staying curious, moving quickly, and solving everyday challenges in smart, practical ways. Backed by W.W. Grainger and inspired by our endless assortment business model, we’re on a clear path toward our next big milestone: $2 billion in revenue—and beyond.

At Zoro, we don’t just follow a playbook—we help build it. You’ll get to work on real problems with a supportive team that shares ideas freely, learns from each other, and celebrates wins together. Our culture is grounded in values that guide how we show up every day: Winning & Learning Together, Being Customer Obsessed, Being Transparent, and Taking Ownership. We don’t have all the answers, but we’re always asking good questions.

Zoro’s culture has been recognized by Fortune, Best Places to Work, and Built In Chicago—but the recognition we care about most comes from our team members, who make this place what it is.

We also know that flexibility matters. Our hybrid work model gives you space to focus and the flexibility to live your life — asking team members to be onsite at least two days a week. Our Chicago HQ (right above Ogilvie Transportation Center in the Accenture Tower) is always open and ready for connection, collaboration, or just a good cup of coffee.

At Zoro, we’re growing fast toward big aspirations — and we’re continuously excited about the new challenges we get to solve together.

  • Professional Development: $1,000.00 CEU stipend and additional PTO time for conference attendance, Career pathways for leadership in a rapidly growing company, Weekly clinical meetings, and collaboration with an interdisciplinary team.

What you will do as a BSC:

  • Conduct initial and follow-up behavior assessments with patients.
  • Provide consultation and training to parents, school personnel and BHT/BHT-ABA.
  • Generate initial behavior assessment reports and treatment plans in compliance with insurance and organization standards.
  • Conduct Functional Behavior Assessments and develop and implement behavior intervention plans.
  • Participate in psychological evaluations.

What you will bring to the team:

  • Master’s degree in Behavior Analysis, psychology, special education, social work, counseling, or related discipline.
  • Behavior Specialist Licensure.
  • 2+ years of experience working with individuals diagnosed with an autism spectrum disorder.

Working Conditions and Physical Demands:

  • This job operates in a clinic, home, or school environment and routinely uses standard office equipment such as a computer/tablet and phone.
  • Ability to lift 50 lbs. and perform tasks involving verbal communication and physical activity, which may include prolonged periods of walking, running, standing, bending, kneeling, squatting, climbing, and stooping.


About the company:

NeurAbilities Healthcare is a distinguished specialty healthcare provider with a team that constantly seeks new and innovative ways to provide the best possible care for patients. Founded by a neurologist who put his vision of compassionate, high-quality patient care into practice, we remain on a mission to transform the lives of individuals with autism and other neurodevelopmental disabilities in New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and beyond. title: MLT Instructor - Abbotsford
description:
Job Description

Western Community College is a privately held provider of post-secondary education in British Columbia, offering a Bachelor of Hospitality Management degree program and more than 67 career training diploma and certificate programs in the fields of business, accounting, healthcare, education, hospitality, information technology, legal studies, and warehousing, using industry-based, market-driven curricula. Western Community College has been a pioneer in offering various healthcare programs. WCC invites applications from eligible and experienced candidates for the position of Instructor – Medical Laboratory Assistant

Program (Laboratory Sections).


Position Overview – MLT Instructor

WCC is seeking qualified and experienced Medical Laboratory Technologists (MLTs) to support the delivery of specific laboratory sections within the Medical Laboratory Assistant (MLA) Program.


The initial need for this position is primarily for a limited number of courses or laboratory sections per cohort, and the position will therefore be offered on a casual, course-by-course basis. The successful candidate may be scheduled for selected courses or laboratory sessions based on program requirements and their availability.

The position is primarily required at the Abbotsford Campus. However, depending on the candidate’s availability and willingness to travel, there may also be opportunities to teach at nearby WCC campuses, such as Surrey and Agassiz, based on course scheduling and program needs.


Candidates who have greater availability may have the opportunity to teach additional courses within the MLA Program beyond the initial assignment.


Initial Teaching Assignment

  • Employment Type: Casual / Course-by-Course
  • Primary Location: Abbotsford Campus, British Columbia
  • Potential Additional Locations: Nearby WCC campuses, including Surrey and Agassiz, subject to availability, scheduling, and program needs
  • Initial Assignment: For the next cohort, MLT laboratory instruction is expected to be required from January 4, 2027, to February 10, 2027, 5.5 hours per day, 27.5 hours per week.
  • Additional Teaching Opportunities: May be available depending on the instructor’s availability, qualifications, course scheduling for future cohorts, enrollment, and program requirements.


Responsibilities

  • Deliver laboratory instruction for designated courses within the Medical Laboratory Assistant Program.
  • Provide hands-on instruction and demonstrations of relevant laboratory procedures, techniques, and practices.
  • Support students in developing the practical skills and competencies required for medical laboratory assistant practice.
  • Ensure laboratory instruction is delivered in accordance with applicable professional, safety, and institutional standards.
  • Provide clear instructions, demonstrations, guidance, and feedback to students during laboratory activities.
  • Evaluate student performance and provide constructive feedback as required.
  • Maintain a safe, professional, respectful, and supportive laboratory learning environment.
  • Support student learning and respond appropriately to questions and individual learning needs.
  • Collaborate with the MLA Program team and other instructors to ensure consistency and quality in course delivery.
  • Maintain required attendance, assessment, and academic records.
  • Contribute to curriculum and laboratory course improvement as required.
  • Stay current with developments, practices, and standards relevant to the medical laboratory profession.
  • Participate in professional development and other academic activities as required.


Qualifications

  • Certified Medical Laboratory Technologist (MLT) in good standing with the Canadian Society for Medical Laboratory Science (CSMLS).
  • Demonstrated experience working in a medical laboratory setting, with at least 2 years of recent work experience in the field.
  • Previous teaching, training, or instructional experience is preferred.


Scheduling and Future Teaching Opportunities

The initial requirement is for a limited number of laboratory courses or sections per cohort. As a result, the number of hours and teaching assignments may vary throughout the academic term, and there may be periods when no teaching is scheduled.


Depending on the instructor’s availability, qualifications, enrollment, course scheduling, and program needs, additional courses or laboratory sections may be assigned within the MLA Program.


Work Locations

The primary need for this position is at the Abbotsford Campus.

Where feasible, and depending on the instructor’s availability and willingness to work at other locations, teaching opportunities may also be available at nearby WCC campuses, including Surrey and Agassiz.


Benefits

  • Extended health care
  • Vision care
  • Dental care

title: Program Director
description:
Refuge for Women is a non-profit, faith-based organization providing specialized care for women who have escaped human trafficking or sexual exploitation. With multiple locations across the U.S., Refuge for Women offers safe housing, at no charge to the resident, with around-the-clock care as clients progress through evidence-based, trauma-informed programming. The compassionate staff is trained to help residents work through the program to reclaim their identities and reach their goals to overcome addictions, heal from trauma and develop life skills leading to healthy, balanced living and financial independence. Refuge for Women strives to help each woman complete the program with a vision for her future, equipped to succeed and sustain a life marked with dignity and hope.


Refuge for Women is a faith-based organization and it is important for staff to share the same basic values and expectations held by Refuge for Women. We require that all staff are believers in Jesus Christ. Read our Statement of Faith.


Must be able to successfully pass a background check and drug test upon receiving an offer of employment.


To view Refuge for Women's benefits, click HERE.


Position Overview:

The Program Director oversees and directs staffing, administration and execution of the program and house operations in accordance with the mission, values and goals of Refuge for Women. This position supervises program staff and volunteers to help conduct and coordinate day-to-day program and house activities with the residents. The Program Director models healthy and loving relational boundaries in a home environment as residents heal and learn successful life skills.


Your team contribution:

The Program Director leads the charge in terms of running a Refuge for Women home. This position is responsible for both leading the team of program house employees as well as overseeing the residents as they progress through the program. The Program Director sets the tone for how a home runs.


You’ll be successful if:

You love leading a team, and at the same time, are able to connect one-on-one and meet women where they are in their recovery. This position flexes between both the big picture goals of the home and the individualized care we provide to residents. You hold firm boundaries and know when to be tough and when to be tender.


Program Responsibilities:

  • Review applications and conduct interviews with potential residents
  • Direct the intake process and oversee orientation period of new residents
  • Direct programming and scheduling of day-to-day activities with the residents
  • Oversight and/or direct involvement in crisis situations with residents
  • Work with other staff, volunteers or Direct Care Associates to schedule residents’ appointments and arrange transportation for medical, recovery meetings, church, grocery shopping, training and employment activities
  • Work with staff and volunteers to plan activities and find individual volunteers as needed for transportation, teaching classes or other house operations
  • Coordinate and consult with other Program Directors to ensure smooth transition of residents to the next phase

title: Sr. Software Engineer (Data & Integrations Engineering)
description:
Our healthcare system is the leading cause of personal bankruptcy in the U.S. Every year, over 50 million Americans suffer adverse financial consequences as a result of seeking care, from lower credit scores to garnished wages. The challenge is only getting worse, as high deductible health plans are the fastest growing plan design in the U.S.

Cedar’s mission is to leverage data science, smart product design and personalization to make healthcare more affordable and accessible. Today, healthcare providers still engage with its consumers in a “one-size-fits-all” approach; and Cedar is excited to leverage consumer best practices to deliver a superior experience.

The Role

We are seeking a seasoned Sr. Software Engineer to join our Data & Integrations Engineering team on the Integrations Engineering squad to integrate with new client systems and enhance the integrations of our live clients.

This team owns implementations, migration, and live integration support for the flagship Cedar Pay product. You will be partnering closely with Data & Integrations Platform, Product, Delivery, and Support. This is a dynamic role that focuses on both refining and enhancing our critical integrations and on strategic investments in our core data pipelines through data semantics, 835 processing, and data catalog and lineage.

In this role you will:

  • Lead the design, implementation, and evolution of the interfaces that connect live integration data to the rest of Cedar.
  • Serve as a product engineer for internal users, driving the roadmap and delivering tools and data abstractions that make messy, customer-sourced data understandable and consumable across the company.
  • Support our existing live clients by implementing strategic enhancements to their integrations.
  • Act as a technical mentor for the team, establishing coding standards and best practices for our evolving data platform.
  • Balance delivery on the needs of today while keeping an eye toward our future North Star Architecture, grounding deliverables in business critical outcomes with strong engineering fundamentals
  • Collaborate closely with delivery engineering teams on mechanisms to improve the quality, speed and scalability of data integration with healthcare providers.
  • Continuously drive scalability into data tools, processes and engineering practices in order to reduce implementation and analytic timelines, customer friction points and maintenance costs.
  • Apply rigorous software engineering practices to the data domain, including version control, automated testing (unit/integration), CI/CD, and structured logging/observability.

Who You Are:

  • 6+ years of professional software development experience, ideally in data/system integrations roles.
  • Experienced in designing systems with real-world scale, complexity, and ambiguity.
  • Strong communicator who collaborates well with cross-functional teams and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Skilled in mentoring peers and helping others grow through pairing, feedback, and guidance
  • Comfortable with tradeoffs and pragmatic about architecture decisions.
  • Passionate about improving the healthcare experience through thoughtful, human-centered software.

Bonus Points For:

  • Comfort with Python/Django
  • Experience with Healthcare Interoperability Standards such as HL7/FHIR, X12, etc.
  • Technical expertise across the data ecosystem: storage, query and ETL orchestration technology; governance and quality; analytics, visualization, and AI/ML pipelines.
  • Familiar with data engineering paradigms like ETL, ELT, Medallion Architecture, and Data Mesh, and can reason between them.
  • Strong self-starter with initiative. Cedar is a mature startup, but successful candidates will still need a strong drive to understand the systems and navigate them to deliver successfully.
  • Familiarity with data engineering tools like dbt, Snowflake, Apache Airflow, Dagster, SQL Alchemy, Fivetran, and Kafka.
  • Familiarity with Kotlin and Go.

Compensation Range and Benefits

  • Salary/Hourly Rate Range*: $195,500 - $247,250
  • This role is also bonus and equity eligible
  • This role offers a competitive benefits and wellness package

What do we offer to the ideal candidate?

  • A chance to improve the U.S. healthcare system at a high-growth company! Our leading healthcare financial platform is scaling rapidly, helping millions of patients per year
  • Unless stated otherwise, most roles have flexibility to work from home or in the office, depending on what works best for you
  • For exempt employees: Unlimited PTO for vacation, sick and mental health days–we encourage everyone to take at least 20 days of vacation per year to ensure dedicated time to spend with loved ones, explore, rest and recharge
  • 16 weeks paid parental leave with health benefits for all parents, plus flexible re-entry schedules for returning to work
  • Diversity initiatives that encourage Cedarians to bring their whole selves to work, including three employee resource groups: be@cedar (for BIPOC-identifying Cedarians and their allies), Pridecones (for LGBTQIA+ Cedarians and their allies) and Cedar Women+ (for female-identifying Cedarians)
  • Competitive pay, equity (for qualifying roles), and health benefits, including fertility & adoption assistance, that start on the first of the month following your start date (or on your start date if your start date coincides with the first of the month)
  • Cedar matches 100% of your 401(k) contributions, up to 3% of your annual compensation
  • Access to hands-on mentorship, employee and management coaching, and a team discretionary budget for learning and development resources to help you grow both professionally and personally

About us

Cedar was co-founded by Florian Otto and Arel Lidow in 2016 after a negative medical billing experience inspired them to help improve our healthcare system. With a commitment to solving billing and patient experience issues, Cedar has become a leading healthcare technology company fueled by remarkable growth. "Over the past several years, we've raised more than $350 million in funding & have the active support of Thrive and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z).

As of November 2024, Cedar is engaging with 26 million patients annually and is on target to process $3.5 billion in patient payments annually. Cedar partners with more than 55 leading healthcare providers and payers including Highmark Inc., Allegheny Health Network, Novant Health, Allina Health and Providence.

title: Central Load Planning Agent, Amazon Air Network Control Center
description:
Amazon Air's Centralized Load Planning team is looking for detail-oriented aviation professionals who
are passionate about operational safety and accuracy as we continue delivering smiles to Amazon
customers every day.

As a Centralized Load Planning (CLP) Agent, you will be directly responsible for the accuracy of the
information provided to Amazon's air carriers relating to aircraft loading. This includes aircraft weight
and balance calculations, Unit Load Device (ULD) container weights, and fuel load.

The CLP Agent will assign positions for all containerized, palletized, and loose outbound cargo and communicate any concerns to local gateway teams if adjustments are required. The CLP Agent will understand weight and balance theory and adhere to aircraft operator and manufacturer requirements.

Applicants are required to successfully pass all company initial certifications and maintain all required certifications during annual recurrent training in areas of load planning responsibilities.

This position requires strong communication with operational leaders, executive leaders, corporate
managers, technical product managers, airline carrier partner leadership, and third-party vendors.
Serving as a subject matter expert, the CLP Agent provides the CLP team with regulatory knowledge,
expertise, and practical experience in the areas of load planning, cargo buildup, and aircraft weight and
balance systems.


Key job responsibilities
- Deliver load planning guidance for complex, multi-flight operations while communicating container inventory, special loads, DG, and aircraft-specific instructions to gateways and stakeholders.
- Utilize advanced technical knowledge and judgement of load planning to navigate complex and ambiguous operational scenarios
- Communicate, provide direction and guidance to Gateway Operations Leaders to ensure aircraft load accuracy in accordance with the load plan.
- Provide mentorship to gateway operations as needed.
- Ensure creation/distribution of weight and balance calculations to flight crew members, be able to navigate complex scenarios with partner carrier flight operations/leadership.
- Utilize Amazon Air systems for overseeing load planning operations per assignment and provide operational improvements/designs to support teams. - Provide operational SME expertise to local gateways, NCC operations and carrier partners.
- Ensure accurate production of assigned load plan and manages workload to include review of planned payload, required weights, fuel, ULD types, loading needs of assigned location.

title: Senior Estimator – Industrial Fabrication
description:
Senior Estimator –
Industrial Fabrication

Build reliable labour and material estimates from fabrication knowledge and project results.

LOCATION

Suite 240, 4000 Glenmore Court SE
Calgary, AB T2C 5R8

REPORTS TO

Applications Engineering Manager

TEAM

Applications Engineering, Production
and project execution teams

BUSINESS

Design-Build

Who you are

You understand how work moves through a fabrication shop and what it takes to estimate it accurately. You bring practical knowledge of labour, materials and production methods, and want to turn that experience into estimating tools that people can trust.

In Design-Build, you’ll develop and improve labour and material estimating tools for packaged gas processing and refrigeration systems. You’ll compare estimates with completed project results, identify productivity patterns and apply those lessons to the next bid. Your contribution will help Applications Engineering prepare more accurate bids and Production plan with better information.

You’ll work with Applications Engineering, Production and project execution teams to turn shop knowledge into usable rates, allowances and templates. As one of Startec’s Everyday Mavericks, you’ll ask practical questions, communicate clearly and take responsibility for accurate, consistent information that colleagues can use.

What you bring

Required technical experience

  • More than 5 years of experience in estimating, estimation coordination, fabrication operations or manufacturing coordination.
  • Strong understanding of fabrication processes, labour productivity and material management.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including formulas, pivot tables and data analysis.
  • Experience with estimating software, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems or production tracking tools.

Analytical skills and working approach

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to accuracy and consistency.
  • Excellent organizational and communication skills, and the ability to collaborate across departments.
  • A self-motivated approach and a continuous improvement mindset.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Assets:

  • A diploma or degree in Engineering Technology, Construction Management, Manufacturing or a related field is preferred. Equivalent fabrication shop or estimating experience may be considered.
  • Experience in fabrication shops handling components such as piping, structural steel, rotating equipment and pressure vessels/exchangers is preferred.
  • Experience developing estimating spreadsheets, databases or productivity tracking tools is highly desirable.

Why Startec Thermal and Process

Founded in 1976, Startec is one of the most trusted names in fit-for-purpose thermal and process solutions. With a team of over 300, we offer full asset lifecycle services, including: upfront system engineering and design, equipment fabrication, maintenance, repair and optimization to organizations across North America.

We serve as specialist partners expanding the expertise and capacity of industrial operators, new project development teams, engineering firms, and equipment manufacturers.

Sectors of focus include oil & gas, renewable energy, mining, industrial gases, petrochemicals, data centers, food and beverage, cold storage, and recreational ice facilities.

What you’ll be responsible for

Estimating Tool Development & Maintenance 30%

Estimating Models & Databases

Develop, maintain and continuously improve fabrication and assembly labour estimating models and databases for shop activities. Create and manage material estimating tools for piping, structural and miscellaneous fabrication. Maintain estimating data libraries, production rates, labour curves and unit-rate databases.

Standardization & Estimating Tool Updates

Standardize estimating templates, workflows and calculation methods. Update tools using actual shop productivity, lessons learned and changes in fabrication practices.

Data Analysis & Reporting 25%

Performance Analysis

Analyze historical project performance to validate and improve estimating accuracy. Track labour productivity metrics and material consumption trends. Support benchmarking and continuous improvement within fabrication operations.

Estimate Accuracy & Reporting

Measure labour and material estimate accuracy against actual project performance. Provide clear, timely reporting on estimating data, trends and improvement opportunities.

Collaboration & Operational Support 25%

Cross-Functional Coordination

Gather estimating inputs from fabrication teams. Work closely with Applications Engineering, Production and project execution teams to support consistent estimating practices.

Bid & Production Support

Provide labour-hour and material estimates for bid preparation. Assist with production planning and forecasting as required. Participate in post-project reviews to compare estimated and actual performance.

Systems & Process Improvement 15%

Digital Tools & Automation

Assist with implementing and optimizing estimating software and digital tools. Improve automation and data integration within estimating processes.

Documentation & Best Practices

Keep estimating documentation, databases and records accurate and current. Support the development of estimating best practices and standard operating procedures.

Ready to apply?

All applicants must complete the TRAITS Behavioural Assessment when submitting their application.

Complete the TRAITS Assessment

We offer competitive wages, training, flexible, dynamic, and exciting work environment.

We thank you for your application and interest in our organization. Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Beast Industries is a multifaceted media and entertainment company founded by Jimmy Donaldson, popularly known as MrBeast, the most watched person in the world. About the Role
Beast Industries is building a new consumer app and we are hiring for a Principal Product Manager to set product direction for the internal tools that support and safeguard members: the consoles, queues, and automation our agents and investigators use every day.

What you'll own:
Own the product roadmap and requirements for operations tooling: agent, analyst, investigator consoles, case management, moderation review queues, escalation routing, data access and deletion workflows, and reporting.

Own the requirements for the case management and enforcement tooling that integrity investigators use: one-click actions connected to the app backend (lock an account, force ID verification, hold a payout), bulk actions across linked accounts surfaced through a network view, restricted states for ambiguous cases (a member can still play but can't touch prizes or balances), and an audit log of who took each action and why.

Build the identity and enforcement tooling that keeps bad actors out: give investigators the signals to catch fraud, bots, cheaters, and banned users returning on alternate accounts, and own the challenge and verification UX members see when flagged.

Own the appeal path for age-band decisions: how decisions are appealed and overturned, including the console tooling an agent uses to change an age band after a successful appeal.

Partner with legal and operations to define data standards for age and identity decisions: what we need to send to and receive from the external vendor on each decision (method used, result, appeal outcome) in order to operate our product safely and securely and in compliance with applicable regulations.

Make build-vs-buy calls with Engineering and Operations leadership across the support platform, identity and consent vendors, case management and enforcement tooling, and moderation.

Partner with Operations to define where automation acts and where a person reviews. Set the thresholds, fail-safe behavior, audit trail, and appeal path for each automated decision.

Work with Product Policy and Legal to turn rules and regulation into requirements Engineering can build, keeping a clear line from each external rule to the shipped feature.

Establish the metrics that matter for customer support (e.g. deflection, resolution time, CSAT, appeal overturn rate) and platform integrity (e.g. fraudulent payout rate, time to detect, chargeback rate), and the data and dashboards needed to evaluate the customer experience.

Sequence the work with Engineering against launch, and say early when something won't fit.

Run beta and launch readiness for these surfaces, including what support and operations need on day one.

What you'll bring:

10+ years in product management, with a record of leading large, ambiguous, cross-functional work from concept to measurable impact.

Experience owning internal tools or platform products that operations teams rely on every day, and the habit of designing for those users.

Hands-on product experience with identity, age assurance, or consent flows in a consumer product, including how completion rates differ by method and market.

Working knowledge of children's privacy and safety rules. COPPA or comparable minor-safety experience is a strong plus, given who our members are.

Experience getting a consumer app through app store review, ideally with features involving prizes, payments, or younger users.

Trust and safety or support tooling experience: moderation workflows, case management, and enforcement systems.

Build-vs-buy judgment, including deep third-party integrations through APIs and webhooks.

Enough technical fluency to read API documentation, scope an SDK integration, and partner with engineering on sequencing work.

Clear writing, including PRDs engineers build from, and the ability to explain tradeoffs to operations, policy, and legal.

Nice to have:
Applied AI experience in support or safety: LLM-assisted triage and decision support, with evaluation and guardrails.

Experience with vendors like Helpshift, Zendesk, Sierra, Decagon, Cinder, Arkose, Zentropi, Musubi, Sift or other CX, fraud, and safety vendors.

Experience with age assurance or consent vendors such as k-ID and Persona.

Experience with sweepstakes, contests, or gaming.

Experience with live, real-time environments.

Location: Bay Area - Reporting To: Director of Product: $235k - $300k base + equity + benefits

TULIP was founded out of the MIT Media Lab. It is headquartered in Boston, has offices in Munich, Tokyo, Tel Aviv, Budapest and Singapore, and has customer sites in more than 45 countries.

DACH is the heart of global manufacturing. Germany is Europe's largest industrial economy and the birthplace of Industrie 4.0. Switzerland is a global centre for pharma, life sciences and precision manufacturing. Austria is a strong base in automotive, machinery, metals and semiconductors. We are now hiring a Managing Director (Geschäftsführer, m/w/d) of TULIP GmbH, who will also be TULIP’s Commercial Leader for DACH. title: Program Advocate (Anchor Village) PT - Sat & Sun 3pm-11pm
description:
Program Advocate (Anchor Village) PT

In-Person Full-Time (16 hours per week) Position in Alameda, CA (Non-Exempt)

Who We Are

Ruby's Place dba Restorative Pathways (RP) is an innovative nonprofit committed to ending domestic violence, human trafficking, and violent crime through hope, advocacy and connection. Our services include emergency shelter, transitional housing, rental subsidies, mental health services, substance recovery, and wrap-around services. All our services are trauma-sensitive and client-centered and are provided at no cost to our clients. All programs are low barrier.

RP is led by survivors with a focus on reflection, innovation, and connection. We believe in fostering relationships, both in our direct service work and throughout our internal work culture. We aim to cultivate a workplace that appreciates and emphasizes the voices of those most impacted by violence. We recognize these voices are vital to interrupting the cycle of violence and transforming lives towards safety, unity, and trust.

Who You Are

You have a strong commitment to preventing interpersonal violence as well as an understanding of, and sensitivity to, serving diverse populations. You have excellent interpersonal skills and strong techniques for relationship building. You believe people should determine their own path towards healing, and have an orientation towards survivor-centered services.

You are a go-getter who enjoys fast paced environments. You enjoy working both collaboratively and independently. You are adept at time management and highly organized with a proven ability to ensure you can meet deadlines, plan, organize and execute. You are comfortable working as part of a team and are an accountable collaborator. You excel at organizing, prioritizing, and following through on multiple time-sensitive projects. You are flexible, creative, and take initiative in handling emergencies.

What qualifications are required for this position?

You Are Also:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Experience working with individuals experiencing homelessness or in social service programs preferred.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional in challenging situations.
  • Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team.
  • Experience working in shelters, day centers, or outreach programs.

  • Knowledge of trauma-informed care and de-escalation techniques.
  • CPR/First Aid certification or willingness to obtain.
  • In possession of a valid CA driver's license, proof of insurance, and be approved by RP insurance as a driver in order to drive agency vehicles. If a staff member cannot be approved by RP insurance as a driver, employment might not be able to continue. Instances where staff cannot be approved to drive will be reviewed on a case by case basis to determine if employment can continue in their role without driving agency vehicles. Items considered include but are not limited to: the shift the staff member holds and the frequency/necessity of driving during that shift, the amount of time before the staff member may be approved to drive by the insurance carrier, the availability of other staff on site to drive agency vehicles as program needs require, etc.
  • Able to complete all required background checks. Additional requirements may be deemed necessary, including fingerprinting (Live Scan), completion of all Community Care Licensing (CCL) documents, and ability to meet CCL licensing requirements.

What You Will Do

The Program Advocate serves as a frontline staff member responsible for supporting the daily operations of (Anchor Village) while ensuring a safe, respectful, and welcoming environment for program participants. Advocates provide direct support to individuals accessing services, monitor program spaces, assist with participant needs, and help maintain the overall flow of program activities.

This role requires consistent interaction with individuals experiencing homelessness and housing instability. Advocates play an important role in creating a trauma-informed environment, responding to participant concerns, supporting de-escalation when needed, and connecting participants to available services such as case management and housing navigation. The Program Advocate works closely with the Site Coordinator and other program staff to ensure program guidelines are followed and that participants receive supportive, respectful engagement throughout their time at the program.

Responsibilities include

Direct Participant Support

  • Provide direct support to participants accessing services at Anchor Village.
  • Greet participants, assist with check-in and orientation, and help them understand program guidelines and available services.
  • Respond to participant needs and provide basic information about available resources and supports.
  • Maintain a respectful and welcoming environment for all participants.

Program Monitoring and Safety

  • Monitor program areas to ensure participant safety and adherence to program expectations.
  • Conduct regular site checks and support the maintenance of a calm and organized program environment.
  • Respond to conflicts or concerns among participants using appropriate de-escalation techniques.
  • Report safety concerns or incidents to the Site Coordinator or Program Manager.

Program Operations Support

  • Assist with daily program activities including set-up, service coordination, and participant flow.
  • Support the opening and closing procedures of Anchor Village including the Day Center, Night Shelter, or Safe Parking Program as assigned.
  • Help ensure program spaces remain clean, organized, and ready for participant use.

Documentation and Communication

  • Maintain shift logs and document participant interactions, concerns, and incidents according to program procedures.
  • Communicate relevant updates or concerns to the Site Coordinator and program team.
  • Support documentation processes that contribute to program reporting and operations.

Participant Engagement and Referrals

  • Encourage participants to engage with available services including case management, housing navigation, and supportive resources.
  • Provide referrals and information to participants regarding available services within the program or through community partners.
  • Support participants in accessing services in a respectful and supportive manner.
  • Complete functional timesheets by assigned due dates in compliance with time allocations.
  • Actively participate in reflective supervision sessions.
  • Create and maintain documentation of processes and procedures related to job duties.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Working Conditions

This position requires working directly in program spaces serving individuals experiencing homelessness. Advocates may work day, evening, overnight, weekend, or holiday shifts depending on program needs. The role requires the ability to remain attentive to participant needs while maintaining program safety and operational flow. You must be able to stand for long periods of time and perform physical activities, including lifting up to 25 pounds. You will be subject to frequent interruptions and must be able to multitask and handle stress.

Local travel in the greater Bay Area may be required.

Applying

The pay scale for this role is $26 per hour (non-exempt). The benefits that come with working at RP at part-time hours include immediate vesting in our 403(b) with a generous match. Applicants must be located in the greater Bay Area.

Preference will be given to internal applicants.

If all this sounds like a good fit for you, please submit your resume and, instead of a traditional cover letter, respond to the following prompts:

  • Why do you want to work for RP and why are you a good fit for this role? (200 words max)
  • Using the qualifications listed above (under Who You Are section), please list the top 5 qualification(s) that you feel you currently excel in and 2 qualifications you feel you will need to work toward proficiency. Please provide a brief explanation for each (a few sentences).
  • Briefly describe your experience working directly with individuals experiencing homelessness or in a shelter or service-based program.

title: Senior Producer
description:
Producer (Senior) - Hipster Whale

About Us

At Hipster Whale, we're passionate about creating bright and funny arcade action games that appeal to broad audiences - games that players will continue to enjoy for years to come!

We’re looking for an experienced Senior Producer to join our team in a permanent, ongoing role.This is a highly collaborative role for someone who brings clarity, focus and momentum to game development. You’ll work across multiple projects and disciplines, helping teams plan effectively, make informed decisions, manage risks and deliver high-quality games on time and within scope.

About the Role

You’ll support both new development and live-ops releases across several mobile titles, partnering with a variety of disciplines, platform partners and other stakeholders. You’ll manage schedules and dependencies, keep communication flowing, and help teams stay motivated and focused on shared goals.

The ideal candidate has experience successfully shipping commercial games, strong knowledge of production practices and Agile development, and the communication skills to work confidently with people at every level of an organisation.

This is a full-time, ongoing position. We’re ideally looking for someone based in Melbourne and available to start as soon as possible. Remote arrangements may be considered for the right candidate, with preference given to applicants based locally. Remote candidates should have significant overlap with standard Australian business hours, or be willing to adjust their schedule accordingly. Applicants based in Australia must hold appropriate Australian working rights.

Hipster Whale supports a hybrid working arrangement, with a minimum of two days per week in our Melbourne studio — currently Mondays and Thursdays. We also support flexibility to accommodate individual needs wherever possible.

We’re proud to foster an inclusive and welcoming work environment. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and perspectives.

What You'll Do

  • Own production across multiple projects, including new development and live-ops releases.
  • Create and maintain project plans and release roadmaps, ensuring priorities, milestones, dependencies and key dates are clear and up to date.
  • Help teams prioritise effectively, manage scope and make clear trade-offs between quality, time and resources.
  • Identify risks, dependencies and delivery issues early, then work with teams and stakeholders to develop practical solutions.
  • Facilitate effective communication and decision-making within teams and with external stakeholders. This includes running meetings, documenting decisions and tracking actions.
  • Facilitate collaboration between disciplines and make dependencies visible so teams can work effectively together.
  • Keep Jira and Notion accurate and up to date so they provide a reliable source of truth for roadmaps, tasks, documentation and releases.
  • Facilitate Agile ceremonies, including stand-ups, sprint planning, reviews and retrospectives.
  • Support continuous improvement of our production processes, tools and ways of working.
  • Help create a psychologically safe, collaborative environment where people feel comfortable sharing ideas, raising concerns and taking creative risks.
  • Be a strong advocate for the quality of our games and our team values.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years experience in the games industry or similar, having delivered multiple commercial projects
  • Experience working on mobile games and familiarity with the mobile release processes, including Apple App Store and Google Play
  • A deep understanding of core production principles and practices, including Agile methodologies
  • Excellent communication and facilitation skills, with experience working across disciplines and with stakeholders at all levels of an organisation
  • The ability to identify problems early, communicate them clearly and help teams reach practical decisions
  • Confidence working with schedules, dependencies, project documentation and spreadsheets
  • Experience using task and project management tools such as Jira
  • Enthusiasm for games and a good sense of humour

Bonus Points

  • Experience working on Apple Arcade titles
  • Experience supporting live-ops development, regular content updates or post-launch product development
  • Scrum Master, Agile or project management certification.
  • Professional experience in another game development discipline, such as design, engineering, art, or QA
  • Experience improving production processes, team structures or development workflows
  • Just because we’re calling out for a Producer, doesn’t mean we aren’t extremely interested in hearing about any particular interests you have that may contribute positively to our studio!

Critical Info

  • Competitive salary, based on skills and experience
  • This is a permanent, on-going position.
  • Applications are open until [DATE]
  • We aim to move through the recruitment process as quickly as possible and will respond to all applicants regardless of the outcome.
  • Due to the large volume of applications we receive, we’re unfortunately not able to provide specific feedback to each applicant.

About Hipster Whale

Hipster Whale is a multi-award winning Australian studio, located in the heart of Melbourne.

Their first release, Crossy Road, quickly became a viral success and Hipster Whale titles have amassed more than 500 million downloads to date.

Hipster Whale has joined forces with world-renowned companies along the way, including Bandai Namco and Disney to create more top-charting games like PAC-MAN 256 and Disney Crossy Road.

They continue to make and publish bright and funny games with broad appeal, including Piffle, and the Apple Arcade exclusives Crossy Road Castle and Crossy Road+. Hipster Whale is and is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Atari.

title: Full-Stack Developer
description:
Join Revun as a Full-Stack Developer to scale web applications using cutting-edge technology. Build robust API integrations and enhance coding with AI tools, working in a fast-paced environment.

About Revun

Revun is the software platform and infrastructure layer behind modern property operations. Where other tools solve one piece of the puzzle, Revun unifies leasing, payments, maintenance, communications, compliance, reporting, and brokerage workflows into a single operating system. Owners, property managers, brokerages, leasing teams, maintenance companies, and REITs all operate from the same connected platform, with role-based experiences that adapt to each stakeholder. Based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada.

About the role

As a Full-Stack Developer at Revun, you'll be at the forefront of scaling our web applications. Your day-to-day tasks include reviewing sprint tasks, refactoring backend logic in Laravel, and designing responsive frontends using Tailwind CSS. You will engage with third-party API integration and leverage AI coding assistants to enhance your workflows.

Working closely with the Lead Developer and reporting to the Technical Lead/Founder, your responsibilities include delivering clean, modular code, ensuring zero-downtime deployments, and accelerating development velocity through AI tools. Your success will be assessed by your ability to meet sprint deadlines and ship functional code features consistently.

Within the first 90 days, you'll focus on successfully integrating APIs and leveraging AI tools to accelerate development while maintaining strong code standards. A successful candidate is resourceful, embraces modern coding tools, and communicates progress effectively.

What you will do

title: Weekend Sign Installer - Madison, GA
description:
Directed is seeking an independent contractor to place and pick up temporary weekend signs in the Madison, GA area in the community Madison Hills.

The contractor will be responsible for installing signs between Friday at 5:00 PM and Saturday at 10:00 AM. The same signs must be picked up between Sunday at 6:00 PM and Monday at 8:00 AM. The work may be performed at any time within those windows, as long as all signs are placed by Saturday at 10:00 AM and removed by Monday at 8:00 AM.

The signs are lightweight corrugated plastic, and are installed on wooden stakes. Artisan Direct provides the signs and stakes and provides replacement inventory as needed.

Job Duties:

  • Use Directed's mobile application to report installation and pickup of signs at specific locations
  • Install signs every weekend between Friday 5 PM and Saturday 10 AM
  • Pickup the same signs between Sunday 6 PM and Monday 8 AM
  • Store signs and extra stakes safely during the week
  • Submit a weekly invoice and order replacement inventory after completing pick up- using our website
Pay Information:
  • Starting compensation is $ 82.50 per weekend
  • Pay is issued via direct deposit every two weeks
  • $20.00 Signing bonus
  • $100.00 bonus after 4 weeks of completed work

Requirements

  • Valid driver’s license and current auto insurance
  • 18+ years old
  • Reliable vehicle with enough space to transport 30+ signs
  • A smartphone (Android or iPhone), roughly four years old or newer, capable of running our mobile app
  • Ability to lift and place signs and work outdoors
  • Ability to hammer stakes 6–8 inches into the ground during the first weekend only
  • Dependable and able to complete routes within the required time windows each weekend

Independent Contractor Notice

This is a 1099 independent contractor position. Contractors are not employees of Directed and are responsible for their own fuel, expenses, taxes and insurance. Contractors determine their own driving order, provide their own vehicle and mobile device, and complete the work within the placement and pickup windows provided. No benefits, minimum hours, or employment guarantees are offered. Contractors may accept or decline routes but must complete any route they commit to.

Additional Information

The starting pay is for the current work available in this location. As more work comes available our contractor support team will offer additional work to increase earnings. This role is a great fit for delivery and rideshare drivers, couriers, retirees, veterans, or anyone looking for flexible supplemental income. The work is straightforward, independent, and recurring each weekend. Contractors who enjoy driving, being outdoors, and working solo tend to enjoy this role and find it a dependable way to earn extra income on their own schedule.

title: Business System Lead - People Team and Real Estate
description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The Business Systems team defines and builds the business IT architecture that supports the commercial operation of Waymo's autonomous fleet. The team stands at the intersection of finance, operations and IT; through creative architecture, expertise and attention to detail, it ensures that Waymo has world-class capabilities across all its business processes.
As the Business System Lead for Real Estate and HR, you will serve as a strategic technology partner responsible for building, scaling, and modernizing the enterprise applications powering Waymo’s workforce and workplace solutions. In this role, you will bridge People Operations, Real Estate & Workplace Services (REWS), and Engineering to establish an automated, AI-enabled systems ecosystem. You will lead cross-functional architectures—connecting employee lifecycle events in core HRIS to automated digital identity and physical workplace provisioning—to support Waymo’s commercial and operational scale.
In this hybrid role, you will report to a Senior Manager Sr. Manager Finance, Indirect Procurement & HR Systems.

You will:

  • Portfolio Strategy & Architecture: Define and execute the multi-year technology roadmap across People, Culture, and REWS systems, ensuring alignment between Waymo’s business objectives, IT strategy, and Alphabet corporate infrastructure.
  • Team Leadership & Delivery: Lead, mentor, and guide a high-performing team of systems analysts, engineers, and program managers, driving sprint backlogs, UAT execution, vendor governance, and bi-annual release cycles.
  • Lifecycle Automation: Architect resilient cross-platform integrations translating employee lifecycle events (onboarding, role transfers, departures) into automated downstream actions across identity provisioning, badge access control, and desk allocation.
  • AI-First Solution Design: Modernize core workplace and HR processes by evaluating and embedding AI-native tools, LLM-driven workflow automations, and intelligent business process automation (RPA).
  • Enterprise Systems Integration: Lead large-scale SaaS implementations and platform enhancements anchored around core tools such as Workday HCM, CoStar, Sitetracker, Tririga, and corporate SAP integrations.
  • Operational Excellence & Governance: Direct system change management, 3rd-level incident triage, and root-cause analyses while enforcing enterprise-grade data privacy, audit compliance, and SOC/SOX security controls.

You have:

  • A Bachelor's degree in a technical or business discipline (such as Computer Science, Engineering, Business Administration, or MIS), or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8 to 10 years of experience working as a Business Systems Analyst, specifically supporting corporate HR, facilities/real estate functional areas.
  • Strong understanding of HR & Real Estate tech domain and its core business processes like Hire to Retire.
  • Solid project management fundamentals, including experience working within Agile/Scrum frameworks, managing backlogs, and prioritizing competing requests.
  • Excellent communication skills, with a track record of translating complex technical architecture into plain language for non-technical business partners.

We prefer:

  • Master’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, or an MBA.
  • Deep functional and technical knowledge of Workday (Core HCM, Business Process Framework, Studio, EIB) and enterprise financial/subledger integration points (e.g., SAP).
  • Proven success driving business systems transformation in high-growth technology, autonomous vehicle, or complex hardware/fleet environments.
  • Experience with IoT/sensor-based space utilization systems, lease accounting workflows, and physical security access control integrations (e.g., Lenel, CCure).
  • Practical experience evaluating and deploying generative AI tools, automated chatbots, or agentic workflows to optimize corporate workforce operations.
  • Familiarity with Alphabet internal shared infrastructure, security review standards, and enterprise data privacy policies.

Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for the role location or, if the role can be performed remote, the specific salary range for your preferred location, during the hiring process.

Waymo employees are also eligible to participate in Waymo’s discretionary annual bonus program, equity incentive plan, and generous Company benefits program, subject to eligibility requirements.
