$200,000—$247,000 USD

title: Associate Director - State Policy and Advocacy
description:
The Associate Director of State Policy and Advocacy, supports the Senior Director of State Policy and Advocacy and AKF’s Office of Government Affairs in the development and implementation of state-level public policy efforts across the United States. Reporting to the Senior Director of State Policy and Advocacy, this role covers legislation and regulation in the kidney disease and related health care space across the United States.

The Associate Director of State Policy and Advocacy, advances state legislation and regulations to support and improve policies for kidney disease patients and organ donors, while working to combat legislation that threatens care and access for people with kidney disease. This position works closely with colleagues across the Office of Government Affairs and the AKF Advocacy Network to translate complex health policy issues into effective advocacy that advances AKF’s mission to fight kidney disease and help people live healthier lives.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES


State Government Advocacy – (50%)
This functional area encompasses direct engagement with state lawmakers, agencies, and stakeholders to promote AKF’s state public policy agenda and advance kidney disease policy priorities.

  • Develop working bipartisan relationships with state lawmakers, state agencies, stakeholders, and advocates, including key healthcare policymakers, patient advocacy organizations, state insurance commissioners, and other state agencies overseeing health care programs.
  • Communicate AKF positions strongly and effectively on issues such as charitable premium assistance, transplant and living kidney donors, Medigap, and other issues of importance to AKF and people with kidney disease.
  • Monitor activity in state legislatures and state agencies in the region regarding issues affecting people with CKD and ESRD; assist the Senior Director in efforts to combat legislation that threatens care and access for kidney disease patients. Track ongoing and potential threats to our constituents utilizing state legislative tracking software and record all interactions with legislators and regulators.
  • Collaborate independently with colleagues in the Office of Government Affairs and across the organization to develop grassroots action plans that strategically engage AKF patient-advocates to achieve desired state policy outcomes.

Organizational Support & External Representation (45%)
This functional area covers external representation at state policy conferences, production of advocacy materials, and cross-departmental collaboration to support AKF’s state advocacy efforts.

  • Represent AKF at key state policy conferences, including the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC), the National Council of Insurance Legislators (NCOIL), the Council of State Governments (CSG), and the National Conference of State Legislators (NCSL).
  • Write and send comment letters on behalf of AKF related to state legislation and regulatory activity.
  • Communicate effectively and work closely with colleagues in the AKF Office of Government Affairs, other AKF departments, and the AKF Advocacy Network.
  • Support significant out-of-town travel as required (approximately 40% of position).

Other Duties as Assigned (5%)

  • Additional responsibilities as determined by the Senior Director of State Policy and Advocacy or organizational leadership.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree with a major in Political Science or in a related field.
  • 4–5 years of experience in a similar role with advocacy and state health policy development experience.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Excellent writing, interpersonal, presentation, and communication skills; strong online research skills.
  • Proficient project management skills; well-organized and detail-oriented with excellent proofreading skills; strategic thinker and proactive problem solver able to work independently and within a team framework.
  • Ability to proactively track and coordinate multiple projects and complete work in a timely manner, and communicate across teams the work, its importance, and coordinate cross team collaboration as required.
  • Ability to handle confidential matters with a high level of integrity and demonstrated flexibility.
  • Valid driver’s license; ability to lift 20 lbs; ability to work weekends or evenings as required.

Preferred

  • Specific knowledge of End-Stage Renal Disease, patient access and health insurance issues at the state level.
  • Established relationships with state legislative or agency staff.
  • Experience with Quorum or similar legislative tracking platforms.
  • Demonstrated professional experience working in or supporting public policy, advocacy, government relations, or related initiatives.


COMPETENCIES

  • State Legislative and Regulatory Knowledge
  • Written and Verbal Communication
  • Stakeholder and Relationship Engagement
  • Grassroots Advocacy Coordination
  • Independent Initiative and Self-Direction
  • Project Management and Tracking
  • Adaptability and Problem Solving
  • Mission-Driven and Patient-Centered Focus

The salary range displayed is for a successful candidate hired in the DMV area. The salary range may be adjusted to reflect cost of living factors for candidates living outside of this location.

Employee benefits:

In addition to your competitive salary, paid holidays, vacation, sick and personal days; health, dental, and vision coverage; life insurance and disability coverages; and a generous matching 403(b) retirement plan, we’ll shower you with perks, including:

  • Culture: We ensure our team knows how much they are valued, as demonstrated by our Quality Work Environment (QWE) Task Force and employee-led recognition and social events throughout the year.
  • Compressed work week: Start the weekend early with shorter workdays on Fridays—closing at 3 p.m. from Labor Day to Memorial Day and 2 p.m. in the summer.
  • Flexibility: Employees work from home most of the time with 1-4 days a month in the office.
  • Clear expectations: You’ll know what you need to do to succeed; annual raises and bonuses for all employees are based on your performance.
  • Location: Convenient location and a short walk to the popular Pike and Rose shopping center
  • Parking: Arrive and leave work comfortably, thanks to an underground parking garage whose cost is paid for by AKF. Metro subsidies are provided for those who do not drive.
  • Dress code: Business casual through the week and casual on Fridays.

AKF offers a hybrid work schedule with employees working in the office 1-4 days per month and telework the rest of the time. This position also requires approximately 40% travel.

title: Ground Software Engineer Senior

The Fan Laboratory investigates the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying cancer immunoediting in skin cancer. Current research focuses on understanding the role of natural killer (NK) cells in shaping tumor evolution and controlling cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) progression using molecular, cellular, genomic, and animal model approaches.

title: Tool & Die Maker
description:
Suncast Corporation is the leading US-based designer, manufacturer, and distributor of high-quality resin products for the home and industrial markets. A privately held company headquartered in Western Chicago, Illinois, Suncast prides itself on 35 years of innovation and sustainability across a wide range of product categories with materials proudly sourced in the USA. Everything we do is supported by the strength and ingenuity of American workers and we are committed to helping families across the country make the most of their unique spaces. We utilize state-of-the-art machinery and innovative manufacturing techniques to consistently engineer products of the highest possible quality.

Position Summary:
The Tool and Die Maker repairs and maintains production dies and tooling used in manufacturing. They read blueprints, machine and assemble parts, and make adjustments to keep tools operating properly. This role is also responsible for preparing new dies for production, troubleshooting issues, and ensuring repairs are completed safely and on time.

Responsibilities:

Maintain and repair production tooling while applying proper tool and die knowledge, timing principles, and rework techniques.
Prepare new dies for production.
Review blueprints and other instructions to modify or repair dies as required.
When possible, modify or repair the die while it’s in the press.
Position work for machining and assembly (e.g., using machine tables, chucks).
Select the machine and the machine tool setup for each task.
Select materials for die modifications and repairs.
Disassemble and re-assemble dies as required while inspecting for wear and damage.
Machine parts for die modifications and die repairs while ensuring they meet dimensional and functional requirements.
Test electrical systems and hydraulic systems in the die.
Repair or replace defective components.
Work to ensure modifications and repairs are done within the production deadline.
Check in new dies when received from vendors and complete appropriate procedures and documents.
Report breakdown of root causes, tool damage, and concerns to management.
Lift dies and work pieces in a safe and efficient manner.
Drive a forklift to transport and store dies and follow all safety rules.
Assist with training the less experienced Tool Room employees and evaluate their progress as necessary.
Support and comply with all Suncast safety policies, quality standards, and housekeeping methods at all times.
Perform additional duties as required.

Qualifications:

High school diploma is required.
5+ years of manufacturing experience with 2+ years of experience with stamping dies.
5+ years of experience with stamping dies preferred.
Proficient in operating lathes, milling machines, and electrical discharge machining equipment.
Strong understanding of precision measuring instruments such as calipers, micrometers, and gauges.
Must demonstrate solid mathematical ability, up to trigonometry, for calculating dimensions, tolerances, and material requirements.
Excellent critical thinking skills with a focus on quality and precision.
Experience with CAD software preferred.
Knowledge of programming CNC machines preferred.
Ability to obtain a forklift license.

title: Financial Counselor
description:
A Brief Overview

The Financial Counselor supports customer service, patient financial advocacy, counseling, and clearance activities within Care Connections and Revenue Cycle. This role helps patients understand and manage healthcare costs by providing estimates, collecting pre-service payments, reviewing insurance coverage, facilitating financial assistance and Medicaid enrollment, and arranging payment solutions.

The FC serves as a patient-facing resource, guiding patients and families through financial options while ensuring compliance with healthcare regulations, payer requirements, and UH policies. Responsibilities include financial clearance, eligibility verification, Good Faith Estimates, payment plans, pre-service collections, and support for specialty services.

Working closely with patients, community agencies, insurers, internal departments, and vendors, the FC helps reduce financial barriers to care, improve access to services, and resolve account issues through outreach, reporting, and customer support activities. The role also contributes to process improvements, analytics, patient education, and departmental initiatives.

What You Will Do

Financial Counseling, Financial Clearance & Collections

  • Generate patient estimates and Good Faith Estimates (GFEs) in accordance with organizational and regulatory requirements.
  • Educate patients regarding financial responsibility, deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, and payment options.
  • Conduct pre-service collections, financial clearance activities, and monitor self-pay accounts.
  • Assist patients with payment plans, financing options, and collection of down payments.
  • Review insurance benefits and identify coverage limitations impacting financial responsibility.
  • Counsel patients regarding out-of-network benefits, self-pay obligations, and financial considerations.
  • Conduct specialty-service and IVF financial counseling appointments.
  • Process payments through approved methods.
  • Escalate financially complex accounts for clinical, financial, or operational review.
  • Identify financial solutions that improve financial clearance and patient access to care.

Financial Assistance & Medicaid Support

  • Explain and determine eligibility for hospital financial assistance programs.
  • Assist with financial assistance applications and supporting documentation.
  • Conduct financial hardship assessments and identify available resources.
  • Assist with Medicaid applications, renewals, redeterminations, and eligibility verification.
  • Serve as an Authorized Representative when appropriately designated.
  • Coordinate with county agencies, managed care organizations, government agencies, and community partners.
  • Conduct presumptive eligibility screenings and support enrollment initiatives.
  • Educate patients on available insurance, Medicaid, financial assistance, and community resources.

Customer Service & Patient Engagement

  • Identify patient needs, research issues, and provide solutions and recommendations.
  • Manage inbound and outbound patient financial counseling calls.
  • Support patients with estimates, insurance coverage, payment plans, financial assistance, and billing concerns.
  • Conduct outreach to financially at-risk patients requiring additional support.
  • Coordinate handoffs to Customer Service and appropriate departments.
  • Escalate sensitive patient concerns and promote a positive patient experience through education and advocacy.

Community Outreach, Reporting & Process Improvement

  • Participate in community outreach events, health fairs, and educational initiatives.
  • Support efforts to improve healthcare access and reduce uninsured populations.
  • Analyze reports, worklists, and account inventories to identify improvement opportunities.
  • Assist with implementation of new workflows, best practices, and departmental initiatives.
  • Support leadership with projects, reporting, analytics, training, mentoring, and onboarding activities.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Perform other duties as assigned.
  • Comply with all policies, standards, and departmental procedures.
  • Maintain confidentiality and safeguard Protected Health Information (PHI) in accordance with HIPAA, the UH Code of Conduct, and organizational policies.
  • Maintain compliance with Good Faith Estimate requirements, No Surprises Act regulations, financial assistance regulations, CMS guidelines, Medicaid regulations, and organizational policies related to financial counseling activities.

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
Company Description

Micas Networks is a leading open networking company focused on accelerating data delivery. Catering to the needs of enterprise and cloud data centers as well as hyperscalers, the company’s full portfolio of open networking products including whitebox – bare metal switches, supports various operating systems, including SONiC. Micas also offers comprehensive data center networking switch development services and custom options, leveraging R&D, engineering, and supply chain management expertise along with high-quality and capacity manufacturing capabilities. Micas is set to transform the next-generation Al networking. Our mission is to accelerate our customers' adoption of disaggregated, Al enabling networks. We are committed to innovation, putting our customers first, and operational excellence. We leverage world class partnerships and open-source software to deliver solutions that are both leading-edge and cost-effective.

Job Description

Position Overview

Micas is seeking an experienced Senior Product Manager for data center switching hardware.
This role owns the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for high-performance Ethernet switches used in AI clusters and modern data centers. The position focuses on Broadcom-based switch platforms, CPO architectures, and advanced thermal, power, and liquid-cooling designs, ensuring products meet customer, market, and compliance requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Product Line Strategy

Define and own the long-term vision, strategy, and roadmap for Micas data center switch platforms (e.g., 400G/800G/1.6T). Ensure alignment with business goals, AI and cloud workloads, and hyperscaler requirements. Track product performance, cost, and adoption, and adjust strategy as needed.

Market and Customer Analysis

Analyze data center trends including AI fabrics, scale-out networking, CPO adoption, liquid cooling, and power density growth. Translate customer needs from hyperscalers, CSPs, and OEM partners into clear product requirements and competitive positioning.

Hardware and System Competitiveness

Ensure strong competitiveness across performance, power efficiency, thermal design, reliability, and cost. Drive decisions around Broadcom ASIC selection, port configurations, optics/CPO integration, and system architecture.

CPO, Power, and Thermal Leadership

Own product direction for Co-Packaged Optics (CPO), including OE/RLM management, CMIS alignment, and port-to-engine mapping. Partner with hardware teams on liquid cooling, airflow fallback, power delivery, and thermal margin design for high-power ASIC systems.

Hardware Compliance and Quality

Ensure products meet industry standards and compliance (NEBS, IEC, CE, FCC, RoHS, Telcordia, reliability and stress testing). Work closely with validation teams to drive EVT/DVT/PVT readiness and field reliability.

Cross-Functional Execution

Work closely with ASIC, hardware, firmware, thermal, mechanical, manufacturing, supply chain, marketing, and sales teams to ensure successful product delivery from concept to mass production and customer deployment.

Requirements

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related fields
  • 5+ years of product management experience in networking hardware or data center infrastructure
  • Strong understanding of Ethernet data center switches, Broadcom ASICs, and switch system architecture
  • Working knowledge of CPO, optical modules, CMIS, power delivery, thermal design, and liquid cooling
  • Experience with hardware lifecycle management (EVT/DVT/PVT, compliance, manufacturing ramp)
  • Strong strategic thinking, execution skills, and ability to work across global engineering teams
  • Excellent communication skills with both technical and business stakeholders

title: Software Development Engineer, Annapurna Labs
description:
AWS Networking builds the infrastructure that powers every customer workload in the cloud. ENA Express is a next-generation EC2 networking feature that leverages the Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) protocol - developed by AWS - to deliver industry-leading networking performance: dramatically lower tail latency, higher bandwidth utilization, and consistent packet delivery at scale.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to join the ENA Express team. You will design, build, and own features across the full ENA Express software stack: Firmware on the Nitro-Card, user-space libraries, control plane components, and the performance analytics systems that help our customers get the most out of their network. • Design and develop features across the AWS Networking software stack on Nitro Cards.

• Drive operational excellence: build observability, contribute to on-call health, and lead incident response and post-mortems

We are a team of senior engineers with deep expertise in systems software, networking protocols, and EC2 infrastructure. Our work spans the full stack - from the Firmware on the driver Card, and NIC driver layer up through the EC2 control plane - and we collaborate closely with hardware, firmware, and platform partners. We care deeply about technical craft, operational quality, and each other's growth.

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- Background in systems programming (C / C++) in performance-critical, production environments

- Experience with virtualization (Hypervisors, VMware, Xen), or experience in managing and troublshooting network and experience in Network protocols like DNS/DHCP/TCP

title: Industrial Security Analyst (MDSO)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

INDUSTRIAL SECURITY ANALYST (MDSO)

SpaceX is looking for a multidisciplinary Industrial Security Officer (MDSO) to serve as a Security Analyst within our Washington, DC office. This is a chance to fill a critical role within a dynamic and high-tempo environment working on programs pushing the boundaries of industry and technology. A successful candidate will be a self-starter and problem-solver and will possess the ability to convey security requirements to a diverse group of technical personnel.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own all SCI security aspects within a fast-paced SCIF environment
  • Support FSO in day-to-day collateral security requirements
  • Support all program security aspects of our SCI missions, to include Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), OPSEC plans, PPP’s, DD254’s, etc.
  • Enforce DD254 provisions and own the issuance of subcontractor DD254s
  • Coordinate SCI indoctrinations/debriefings
  • Partner with Mission Management and government representatives to ensure program deliverables are met
  • Create and update all annual refresher, indoctrination, and exit briefings as needed in accordance with policy and government customer requirements
  • Partner with Mission Management and Engineering teams to enhance their understanding of the program classification and other protection requirements
  • Possess a strong understanding of SCG development and the ability to influence customer determinations
  • Maintain accountability of associated program materials
  • Prepare for and successfully execute compliance inspections, including self-inspections
  • Conduct security-related inquiries and incident reporting
  • Keep abreast of the latest security trends and policy updates, implementing innovative solutions and processes
  • Attend and support various customer meetings and working groups

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree; OR 3+ years of security experience performing NISPOM-related security responsibilities in lieu of a degree

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree
  • Strong knowledge of 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM), Intelligence Community Directives (ICDs), and other related security policies and procedures
  • Familiarity with DISS, NBIS, TALON, and Scattered Castles

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

title: Senior Plan Reviewer
description:

They work with architects, engineers, and contractors to ensure alignment with construction codes for structural, mechanical, plumbing, and electrical systems, protecting public safety and ensuring regulatory compliance.

This is a hybrid position that requires in-office attendance at least two (2) days per week at one of our offices in the Northern Virginia / Washington, DC metro area.

  • Review architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, thermal, energy, and fire safety designs for compliance with the International Building Code (IBC), applicable state building codes, national standards, and local ordinances
  • Perform independent calculations to verify performance-based design elements

title: Senior UX Designer (Mobile)
description:
Senior UX Designer (Mobile) - Hipster Whale

About Us

At Hipster Whale, we're passionate about creating bright and funny arcade action games that appeal to broad audiences - games that players will continue to enjoy for years to come!

We're looking for an experienced Senior UX Designer to help us shape and champion excellent player experiences across our titles.

About the Role and Studio

Do you dream in elegant game loops? Do you want a hand-on role where you can play a big part in a relatively small team, working on positively impacting millions of players? Do you want to know why the chicken crossed the road? We’d like to hear from you!

You’ll bring a track record of shipped games (including mobile titles) and a deep understanding of what keeps players engaged. You'll own the UX vision across multiple titles, shaping experiences from quick prototype concepts through to full feature and product rollouts.. This is a hands-on role, and selection will be practical portfolio and communication skill based.

This is a full-time, ongoing position. We’re ideally looking for someone based in Melbourne and available to start as soon as possible. Remote arrangements may be considered for the right candidate, with preference given to applicants based locally. Remote candidates should have significant overlap with standard Australian business hours, or be willing to adjust their schedule accordingly. Applicants based in Australia must hold appropriate Australian working rights.

Hipster Whale supports a hybrid working arrangement, with a minimum of two days per week in our Melbourne studio — currently Mondays and Thursdays. We also support flexibility to accommodate individual needs wherever possible.

We’re proud to foster an inclusive and welcoming work environment. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and perspectives.

What You’ll Do

  • Create, revise, refine and advise on the UX journey and information presentation across the studio’s games
  • Produce wireframes, user flows, prototypes, and high-fidelity mock-ups that communicate design decisions clearly to the team and stakeholders
  • Be able to iterate quickly with MVP visuals, and advise when it’s necessary to add polish or added communication feedback for the evaluation of the UX to be validated
  • Collaborate with the product & development teams to regularly review implemented designs on device and in-engine, test the player experience, and iterate based on design direction, playtesting and analytics
  • Partner with product and creative leadership to identify the right problems to solve, and draw on your knowledge to map and improve the player experience holistically
  • Champion player-centric design principles across the studio and help raise the bar by mentoring the team and sharing your knowledge
  • Participate actively in design reviews, offering considered feedback to others and actively seeking feedback on your own work
  • Help create a psychologically safe, collaborative environment where people feel comfortable sharing ideas, raising concerns and taking creative risks.
  • Be a strong advocate for the quality of our games and our team values.

What We’re Looking For

  • Hands-On Experience - 5+ years of commercial UX design experience, with a portfolio demonstrating meaningful improvements to the player experience that you can talk to. You are comfortable in Figma and other prototyping tools
  • Strong foundational knowledge of design principles - sometimes you break the rules, but it’s not because you don’t know them
  • A love of behavioural Psychology - you love to lock in on player motivations, can watch out for cognitive overload, and you understand the ways to trigger joyful feedback and play loops that drive engagement
  • Understanding of Information Architecture & Interactive Design - you possess a demonstrated ability to clearly present complicated information, a solid understanding of information hierarchy, and able to find the right placement and sequence of delivery - not just on screen layout, but also in flow
  • Knowledge of Accessibility & Usability - you’re thoughtful about physical strain when designing input placements, you tailor design to hardware, and make sure text and cues are readable. You understand not everyone experiences the world the same way, and that our goal is to share our game experiences as widely as possible
  • Game Engine Awareness - basic familiarity with how games are technically held together (if you can get hands-on, all the better)
  • Be a UX Evangelist - Stay current with mobile & games UX patterns, platform developments, and industry best practices, and bring relevant insights back to the team
  • Product Minded - you understand and maintain the various business objectives at play, while working to make amazing experiences for our players. You have a maturity about commercial creativity
  • Collaborative Team Communicator - Experience working cross-functionally, and able to respectfully advocate for design decisions and engage constructively when challenged
  • Player of Games - you play widely and enjoy unpicking emerging trends
  • Good Sense of Playfulness - Alongside the elegant design, you enjoy bringing surprise & delight, and maybe a little silliness to work

Bonus Points

  • UI and graphic design skills (UX is the core function, but being able to illustrate and direct graphic design effectively towards the final execution is highly valued)
  • Experience in User Research sessions and reports

Critical Info

  • Competitive salary, based on skills and experience
  • This is a full-time, on-going position
  • Applications are open until [DATE]
  • We aim to move through the recruitment process as quickly as possible and will respond to all applicants regardless of the outcome.
  • Due to the large volume of applications we receive, we’re unfortunately not able to provide specific feedback to each applicant.

About Hipster Whale

Hipster Whale is a multi-award winning Australian studio, located in the heart of Melbourne.

Their first release, Crossy Road, quickly became a viral success and Hipster Whale titles have amassed more than 500 million downloads to date.

Hipster Whale has joined forces with world-renowned companies along the way, including Bandai Namco and Disney to create more top-charting games like PAC-MAN 256 and Disney Crossy Road.

They continue to make and publish bright and funny games with broad appeal, including Piffle, and the Apple Arcade exclusives Crossy Road Castle and Crossy Road+. Hipster Whale is and is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Atari.

title: Skills Systems Architect
description:
FEQ227R209

About the Role

Databricks needs to understand what technical capability looks like across several large, fast-moving populations: employees, customers, and partners. Today that happens through role-based learning pathways and product-aligned enablement, an approach that can't keep pace with how quickly the platform, technology, and roles change. AI has also collapsed the half-life of technical proficiency, and for the first time, it makes a living, self-maintaining model of capability possible.

In this builder role, you'll own systems for defining, measuring, and developing technical capability across Databricks learner audiences. You'll build a capability model that ties roles, skills, content, and credentials together and the instrumentation that shows where capability actually stands.

What You'll Own

Skills taxonomies, capability models, and learning context

  • Define the skills taxonomies that make up technical capability and shape how they’re organized; what skills exist, which are adjacent, which are prerequisites, how quickly they go stale, and what sources are available to learners for developing and maintaining them.

Observability and measurement

  • Stand up instrumentation and AI-informed signals that show where capability stands and where it's drifting. Develop live signals, not a quarterly or monthly health index, to show how skills are moving and evolving.
  • Anticipate where capability demand is heading. Product releases, market shifts, and role evolution are constant; track changes closely so emerging skills surface early and content and programs stay ahead of change.

AI-native tooling

  • Build the software that maintains the skills taxonomy and capability model, including LLM-driven skill extraction and organization, agentic pipelines that keep them current, automated drift and gap detection, and APIs that expose it all.
  • Make the model reusable enterprise context that other systems, teams, and products build on vs. a training-only asset.

Impact You'll Have

You will sit upstream of and across several teams and functions:

  • Anywhere skills show up in products: You define what technical capability means and what evidence counts, so wherever skills are inferred, captured, or recognized, it reflects real technical work and skills & abilities.
  • Content and curriculum. The skills taxonomy and capability model influence what gets built next and why. Learning context is a critical input to generative content.
  • Learning architecture and in-product training: Your work informs what learning belongs where and how it’s presented. Pathways are assembled with the model and taxonomy instead of mapped by hand; in-product training surfaces them to learners.
  • Certification & accreditation. The capability model grounds skills assessment to guide and accelerate exam developers.
  • Learning & enablement. You give the organization a current view of capability across every audience, and a shared model to build and plan against.

What We're Looking For

  • Experience in technical training, learning, enablement, or product education in data & AI, cloud, or comparable product categories.
  • Experience designing capability or skills models and the systems around them, spanning modeling, measurement, and instrumentation.
  • A builder mindset. Ability to use Python and SQL and build apps, with AI assistance, and wire up pipelines and stand up tooling yourself.
  • AI-native. AI tooling is how you build and reason, from extraction and assessment to agentic workflows and evaluation. You understand when to reach for AI and when not.
  • A track record of moving strategy as an IC through analysis and clear writing.

Nice to Have

title: Manager, Enterprise Service Desk (Tier 1)
description:
Job Summary

The Manager, Enterprise Service Desk (ESD) is a tactical leadership role responsible for the daily execution, management, and enablement of the Tier 1 Enterprise Service Desk staff.

Reporting directly to the Sr. Manager, Enterprise Service Desk, this position focuses on driving the day-to-day operations of the help desk, maintaining high team performance, and directly supporting the front-line technical team. The ideal candidate will bridge technical execution with operational goals, ensuring service delivery remains highly efficient, client-centric, and aligned with organizational standards.

Role Focus

The primary focus of this role is to champion continuous improvement and alignment with the company’s strategic vision, cultivating an empowered team culture through highly skilled coaching and structured mentorship, while driving execution around rigorous KPI standards, systemic efficiency, white glove customer service, and top-tier client escalation resolution.

Responsibilities

Team Leadership and Management

  • Staff Oversight: Manage, coach, and support the Tier 1 service desk staff to maximize operational readiness and career pathing
  • Talent Development: Oversee the onboarding process for new hires and coordinate continuous technical and customer-service training to ensure up-to-date skillset alignment.
  • Performance Accountability: Conduct structured performance reviews, lead daily operational huddles to check on backlog progress, and proactively resolve internal roadblocks.
  • Workforce Management: Design, implement, and maintain complex multi-shift team schedules to ensure stable, cost-effective coverage across all active client service windows.

Performance and Quality Assurance

  • Target Enforcement: Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and service level agreements (SLAs) constantly to ensure team performance targets are met quickly and effectively.
  • Quality Assurance Auditing: Conduct regular ticket, phone call, and live chat evaluations to maintain exceptional quality standards, professional etiquette, and precise technical documentation.
  • Metric Reporting: Synthesize raw ticketing data into meaningful daily and weekly operational performance reports to present to clients and senior leadership.

Client Relationship and Escalation Management

  • Incident Management: Act as the main tactical point of contact for handling complex technical issues and client-facing escalations.
  • Relationship Management: Build and maintain active, positive relationships with critical client contacts, leveraging post-incident surveys and verbal feedback to address underlying concerns.
  • Communication Bridge: Serve as a seamless, high-clarity communication link between technical support personnel and client business stakeholders, driving problems to full resolution.

Strategic & Operational Oversight

  • Process Improvement: Identify workflow inefficiencies and knowledge base gaps, continuously updating internal standard operating procedures (SOPs) to optimize the overall support process.
  • Client Onboarding: Assist with the practical technical and operational onboarding of new customer accounts into the Tier 1 Service Desk ecosystem.
  • Incident Preparedness: Participate actively in a regular management on-call rotation for high-severity major incidents and attend leadership strategy meetings to align on departmental goals.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • SLA Adherence: Maintain >95% (or corporate target) compliance on initial response and overall resolution times across all active tiers.
  • First Contact / First Touch Resolution (FCR / FTR): Optimize front-line handling mechanics to consistently maximize first contact / touch resolutions and lower overall escalation ratios.
  • Quality Assurance (QA) Score: Ensure team call, chat, and documentation audit scores average at or above targeted departmental baselines.
  • Team Utilization: Track active agent productivity (time spent resolving tickets, on calls, or in chat channels) against scheduled availability to maintain cost-efficiency.
  • Customer Satisfaction (CSAT): Maintain high transactional customer satisfaction scores across all closed team incidents.
  • Throughput & Team Velocity: Track and drive individual and team metrics for tickets handled and closed per hour to maintain high-efficiency output and prevent backlog stagnation
  • Call Handle Ratios & Abandonment Rates: Manage real-time queue performance to ensure the ratio of incoming interactions to successfully completed calls meets established corporate thresholds.
  • Knowledge Base (KCS) Contribution: Measure the team's active creation, updates, and utilization of internal troubleshooting documentation to foster a culture of continuous learning and support self-service enablement.

KPIs metrics to be developed, tracked, and reviewed as part of continuous improvement

Skills

  • ITSM & Tools Proficiency: Comprehensive hands-on experience with enterprise management tools including Connectwise, ServiceNow, and Contact Center Platforms (RingCentral).
  • Operational Metrics Design: Advanced capability to analyze ticket analytics, track business hour conversions, and construct data-driven reporting metrics.
  • Process Engineering: Strong foundational expertise in ITIL framework, SLA architecture, and incident management workflows.
  • Strategic Team Building: Proven track record of managing scaling operations and executing performance optimization initiatives.
  • Workforce Management (WFM): Proficiency in utilizing forecasting tools and data to design optimized shift schedules, managing queue coverage across multiple time zones, and ensuring sufficient resource allocation.
  • Knowledge Management Governance: Expertise in designing and maintaining a Knowledge Centered Service (KCS) architecture to empower agent learning, document technical solutions, and support self-service enablement.
  • Performance Coaching & Mentorship: Demonstrated mastery of structured coaching frameworks to identify performance gaps, deliver actionable real-time feedback, and foster the career development of front-line technicians.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and hands-on professional IT management experience.
  • ITIL certification or equivalent service management qualification required.
  • 5+ years of experience in IT service delivery or technical customer support environments, with at least 2–3 years in a direct supervisory, shift lead, or team management capacity.
  • Experience in an MSP, healthcare, financial services, or other complex client-facing support environment strongly preferred.

The Benefits of Working for Abacus

  • Exposure to a diverse array of technologies
  • Part of a team of experienced technicians that aim to deliver exceptional services.
  • Competitive compensation
  • Robust benefits package: medical, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, 401k, and PTO
  • Opportunities to further technical education through Employee Certification Program
  • Positive, friendly, supportive office environment
  • Workplace perks such as healthy snacks, wellness programs, and fun events

title: Transactions Associate - Los Angeles
description:
Harrison Street Asset Management ("HSAM") is a leading global alternative investment management firm focused on real estate, infrastructure, and credit strategies across North America and Europe. Headquartered in Chicago, Toronto, and London with offices across North America, Europe, Asia and the Middle East, the firm has over $108 billion in assets under management on behalf of institutional investors and registered investment advisors globally.

Founded on a culture of innovation, HSAM is an early mover in alternative real estate and mid-market infrastructure. Today, the firm’s global team, consisting of more than 520 professionals, is committed to creating long-term value through deep sector expertise and forward-thinking strategies.

Harrison Street Asset Management (“HSAM”) is seeking a two-year Associate to join the Transactions team in our New York office. The Associate will play a key role in the evaluation, underwriting, and execution of new real estate investment opportunities across sectors with a focus on major asset classes (multifamily, office, industrial, and retail) as well as exposure to alternatives (senior housing, student housing, medical, and digital). The position will support both equity acquisitions and credit originations efforts on behalf of HSAM’s Transactions team in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. The ideal candidate will be motivated, detail-oriented, and demonstrate a combination of applicable work experience and a passion for real estate investing.

Responsibilities:

  • Support the acquisition and execution of new equity investments across the risk-return spectrum (core to opportunistic) as well as credit originations across the debt capital stack (senior loans, mezzanine loans, public securities, and preferred equity).
  • Develop and maintain detailed financial cash flow models and sensitivity analyses to evaluate potential investments, including valuation, return performance, risk, and capital structuring.
  • Conduct market research, asset-level diligence and comparative operational analyses.
  • Prepare and present in pipeline meetings, deal screening sessions and investment committees, summarizing key underwriting assumptions, loan structure, market, risks and mitigants.
  • Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders, including legal counsel, lenders, and operators, to drive transaction execution from transaction sourcing through closing.
  • Conduct in-depth sector and market research to support investment initiatives and to identify emerging trends and investment opportunities.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Real Estate, Economics, or a STEM-related field with a strong financial analysis record.
  • 3 years of experience in real estate or investment banking, with direct exposure to real estate underwriting and transaction execution.
  • Advanced financial modeling and analytical skills, including proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint; experience with Argus strongly preferred.
  • Highly organized with excellent attention to detail, capable of managing multiple deals and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with ability to synthesize complex analyses into concise recommendations.
  • Self-motivated, collaborative, and intellectually curious, with a demonstrated interest in real estate investing.

title: Fabrication Quality Inspector
description:
Position Summary

Galvan Industries is seeking a hands-on Quality Control Inspector for our structural steel fabrication and metal plate processing shop. This position inspects materials, fabricated parts, welds, and finished assemblies to verify they meet approved drawings, customer specifications, and applicable quality requirements.

The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, comfortable working on the shop floor, and able to communicate quality concerns clearly. This role works closely with production leadership, welders, fabricators, and machine operators to identify problems early, prevent repeat defects, and ensure accurate, complete products are released for shipment.

Key Responsibilities

Material and In-Process Inspection

· Verify incoming steel, plate, and purchased components against order requirements, including dimensions, material identification, and supporting documentation.

· Inspect cut, drilled, formed, and fabricated parts for dimensional accuracy and workmanship.

· Check fit-up, hole locations, alignment, orientation, and assembly dimensions against approved drawings.

· Use tape measures, calipers, squares, weld gauges, and other inspection tools.

· Identify defects early and communicate required corrections before work moves to the next production stage.

Weld and Final Inspection

· Perform visual weld inspections within assigned qualifications and training.

· Check weld size, length, location, and visible workmanship against drawings and established acceptance criteria.

· Verify required inspection checkpoints and documentation are complete before product release.

· Inspect finished assemblies for dimensions, completeness, identification, surface condition, and shipment readiness.

· Coordinate required third-party inspections or nondestructive testing with production leadership.

Documentation and Corrective Action

· Complete inspection reports, checklists, and quality records accurately and promptly.

· Record nonconforming work, identify affected material, and help prevent its unintended use or shipment.

· Verify repairs and rework before releasing affected products.

· Maintain material traceability and inspection records when required by the job.

· Monitor recurring defects and work with production leaders to address their causes.

· Maintain inspection equipment and verify calibration status where applicable.

Teamwork and Safety

· Explain quality expectations to employees and support training on common defects and inspection requirements.

· Follow shop safety procedures and required PPE practices.

· Maintain a clean, organized inspection area.

· Escalate unresolved quality concerns and hold affected work for review under company procedures.

title: Senior Technical Sales Engineer
description:
About SirenOpt

SirenOpt helps manufacturers make better, safer, and more reliable micro- and nano-materials. These materials are the building blocks of critical sectors of the global economy such as batteries, computer chips, aircraft components, and power systems. But, surging material demand and growing complexity are pushing production to unprecedented scales and speeds, leaving manufacturers effectively flying blind. Small, undetected variations during production lead to wastage, lower performance, higher costs, and safety risks.

SirenOpt is changing this by developing a manufacturing intelligence platform that non-destructively probes materials during production, revealing critical internal information without damaging them. Using a novel combination of cold atmospheric plasma, physics-informed machine learning, and predictive analytics, SirenOpt generates unique, real-time material fingerprints that capture material signals not accessible through conventional measurement techniques. These insights give manufacturers unprecedented visibility into how materials behave as they are made.

We turn hidden data into actionable intelligence to help manufacturers reduce variability and thus increase yield and performance. The technology can be deployed as a standalone tool or integrated directly into factory production lines. SirenOpt is currently deploying early versions of its platform with some of the largest industrial manufacturers in the world across North America, Europe, and Asia.

About the job

Job Title: Senior Technical Sales Engineer

Location: On-Site (San Leandro, CA)

Job Type: Full-Time

Role Overview

SirenOpt is hiring a commercially minded Senior Technical Sales Engineer professional to grow adoption of our products. This is one of the most consequential hires we will make: in a deeply technical business, the sales function is where engineering credibility becomes revenue. The person in this role owns that translation turning technical capability into clear customer value and moving quickly from first conversation to a well-scoped sale.

You will work with prospective customers to understand their use case, explain SirenOpt’s technology in practical terms, shape the right deployment solution, and carry opportunities through to close. You will be especially effective with organizations that need a tailored, credible path to evaluating or deploying new technology without a long enterprise sales cycle. Because our customers buy on technical confidence, the quality of these conversations directly determines how fast the company grows.

What You'll Do

  • Build and manage a pipeline for commercial deployments.
  • Identify, qualify, and close opportunities across relevant industrial, research, and operational customer segments.
  • Run discovery conversations that uncover technical requirements, buying context, timeline, and decision-makers.
  • Present SirenOpt’s products and capabilities in a concise, customer-relevant way.
  • Develop proposals, quotes, scopes of work, and deployment plans with internal technical teams.
  • Translate customer needs into clear technical requirements and ensure handoffs are accurate.
  • Lead product demonstrations, pilot discussions, and commercial negotiations.
  • Maintain disciplined opportunity notes, forecasts, and next steps in the CRM.
  • Bring market feedback into product, engineering, and leadership conversations.
  • Represent SirenOpt professionally at customer meetings, industry events, and partner conversations.

What We're Looking For

  • Experience selling technical products, equipment, software-enabled hardware, or engineering services.
  • Comfort engaging both technical users and commercial decision-makers.
  • A practical understanding of consultative sales: discovery, qualification, value articulation, proposal development, and closing.
  • Ability to grasp technical concepts quickly and explain them without unnecessary jargon.
  • Strong written communication, particularly for proposals and customer follow-up.
  • Self-directed, organized, and comfortable owning a deal cycle end to end.
  • Sound judgment around scope, feasibility, pricing, and customer expectations.
  • Willingness to travel occasionally for important customer meetings, demonstrations, or deployments.

Nice to have:

  • Background in optical systems, sensors, scientific instrumentation, industrial technology, robotics, hardware, or related fields.
  • Experience selling benchtop instruments, pilot projects, proof-of-concept engagements, or custom deployments.
  • Existing relationships in SirenOpt’s target markets.
  • Experience working in an early-stage company or small technical team.

What success looks like

Within your first months, you will have built a qualified pipeline, developed a crisp understanding of SirenOpt’s ideal customer and sales motion, and helped close initial benchtop and one-off deployment opportunities. Over time, you will create a repeatable commercial playbook that turns technical interest into well-scoped revenue the foundation the rest of SirenOpt's commercial growth is built on.

Base Pay Range
$130,000—$170,000 USD

Benefits

  • Equity and Salary compensation depends on experience
  • Health, Dental, Vision plans provided
  • 401k matching provided
  • Time off: 20 days of PTO per year, plus approximately 15 paid US holidays per year

title: Senior UX Designer
description:
Position: Senior UX Designer
Client: Labour and Transportation Cluster
Ministry: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement, Ontario
Location: 87 Sir William Hearst Ave., Toronto, ON M3M 0B4
Work Model: Hybrid – 3 days onsite per week, no flexibility
Contract: October 7, 2026 – March 31, 2027
Extension: Up to 135 days; maximum 1 extension term
Openings: 2
Allocation: 100%
Security Clearance: No clearance required
Closing Date: October 9, 2026 at 2:30 PM ET
Position Overview
The Labour and Transportation Cluster is seeking Senior UX Designers to support complex digital products and services through user-centred design, research, prototyping, usability testing, accessibility, and Agile delivery.
The successful candidate will be responsible for applying UX design best practices, mobile-first and responsive design principles, user research, usability testing, prototyping, and iterative design throughout the Ontario Digital Service delivery lifecycle.
The UX Designer will work closely with Product Owners, business stakeholders, developers, technical teams, and other UX professionals within an Agile/Scrum environment and will contribute across the Discovery, Alpha, Beta, and Live delivery phases.
Relationship Management & Stakeholder Responsibilities
The Senior UX Designer must demonstrate strong relationship-management capabilities, including:
  • Communicating effectively with business stakeholders and core project teams.
  • Mediating competing requirements and stakeholder perspectives.
  • Keeping UX activities aligned with project/product schedules.
  • Working effectively with Product Owners, developers, business teams, technical teams, and other stakeholders.
  • Supporting organizational change throughout the delivery lifecycle.
  • Developing strategies and actions to:
    • Overcome resistance to change.
    • Build stakeholder support.
    • Capitalize on forces supporting change.
  • Understanding and contributing to projects across Discovery, Alpha, Beta, Live, or similar delivery methodologies.
  • Working effectively within distributed teams and maintaining regular communication.
Soft Skills
The successful candidate should demonstrate:
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong presentation skills.
  • Ability to clearly explain UX processes, ideas, design rationale, and solutions.
  • Strong interpersonal and negotiation skills.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Strong decision-making skills.
  • Ability to collaborate closely with teams and stakeholders.
  • Ability to work effectively in a distributed/hybrid environment.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and facilitation skills.


Requirements

Mandatory Qualifications / Must-Haves
Candidates must demonstrate the following:
1. UX Design & Responsive Design – Mandatory
  • Extensive experience applying UX design best practices to design digital solutions.
  • Deep understanding and hands-on experience with:
    • Mobile-first design
    • Responsive design
    • User-centred design principles
  • Ability to efficiently and intelligently iterate designs and solutions based on user feedback, research findings, testing, and stakeholder input.
2. Complex Projects & Agile – Mandatory
  • 3+ years of relevant experience participating in complex projects/products of different sizes.
  • Experience ensuring UX activities align with:
    • Project plans
    • UX/design best practices
    • User-centred design processes
    • Agile/Scrum methodologies
  • Experience working as part of a balanced Agile delivery team consisting of Product Owners, UX Designers, developers, and other stakeholders.
3. Communication & Mediation – Mandatory
  • Demonstrated communication and mediation skills when working with business teams and core project team members.
  • Ability to collaborate with stakeholders to ensure client projects/products progress according to schedule.
  • Ability to communicate design decisions, resolve competing requirements, and build alignment among stakeholders.
Education
  • Degree or diploma in Graphic Design is preferred/required as applicable to the candidate's background.
  • Degree or certification in any of the following is considered an asset:
    • Usability
    • Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)
    • Technical Writing
UX Research & Usability Testing
The Senior UX Designer must have experience facilitating User Research and Usability Testing activities.
Experience should include producing deliverables such as:
  • User Interview Topic Maps
  • User Interview Scripts
  • User Interview Synthesis, including collection, aggregation, and analysis of written observations from interviews
  • User Research Findings Reports
  • Usability testing plans and findings
  • Accessibility compliance testing is considered an asset and is specifically required during applicable delivery phases.
UX Tools & Technical Skills
Strong expertise with UX/design tools, including one or more of the following:
  • JustInMind
  • InVision
  • Sketch
  • Adobe Creative Cloud
  • Axure
  • Figma
  • Zeplin
The following technical skills are considered an asset:
  • HTML5
  • CSS3
  • JavaScript
  • React
  • Angular
  • NodeJS
Ontario Digital Service UX Delivery Lifecycle
The UX Designer will produce deliverables across four distinct delivery phases following the Ontario Digital Service Design Playbook.
Phase 1 – Discovery
The Discovery phase focuses on understanding the problem space, business objectives, user needs, and existing solutions before building a product or service.
Responsibilities & Deliverables
Facilitate project kick-off activities and produce outputs such as:
  • Business Model Canvas
  • 5 Whys
  • User Personas
  • Stakeholder Mapping
  • Strategy Map
  • Short- and Long-Term Goals
  • Fears and Challenges
  • Problem Statement
Facilitate user research activities and produce:
  • User Interview Topic Maps
  • User Interview Scripts
  • User Interview Synthesis
  • User Research Findings Report
Support Inception / Science Fair Day, including:
  • Showcasing project work and key findings to stakeholders outside the core project team
  • Aligning business and technical stakeholders on next steps
  • Planning activities for the Alpha phase
Additional Discovery deliverables may include:
  • User Storyboards
  • Technical Service Blueprints
  • Business Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Phase 2 – Alpha
Alpha focuses on testing hypotheses, experimenting with potential solutions, and validating approaches with users before development.
Responsibilities & Deliverables
  • Optionally facilitate or participate in a Google Ventures Five-Day Design Sprint, or an appropriate variation.
  • Create clickable prototypes for multiple potential solutions.
  • Validate clickable prototypes through user usability testing sessions.
  • Produce research findings reports.
  • Iterate and improve prototypes based on research and usability testing findings.
  • Identify existing processes or policies that may need to change to support the proposed product/service.
  • Produce a business proposal supporting funding for the Beta phase.
  • Define a clear vision for the solution to be developed during Beta.
  • Develop a prioritized feature list and plan for Beta.
  • Define the user solution and delivery KPIs.
Phase 3 – Beta
Beta focuses on building and validating a real, user-facing service/MVP based on prototypes tested during Alpha.
The UX Designer will work within a Scrum/Agile methodology and participate in:
  • Daily Stand-ups
  • Sprint Planning
  • Backlog Grooming/Refinement
  • Reporting
  • Acceptance activities
  • Retrospectives
The UX Designer will typically create and validate user stories one iteration ahead of development.
User Story Creation & Validation
For each feature/function, the UX Designer will:
  1. Participate in determining feature priorities.
  2. Facilitate/participate in sketching workshops to visually represent ideas and user flows.
  3. Create UX/UI designs.
  4. Enhance and refine designs.
  5. Conduct user interviews for validation.
  6. Synthesize individual and overall interview findings.
  7. Incorporate research findings into design enhancements.
  8. Obtain Product Owner sign-off.
  9. Add validated stories/features to the backlog for future iteration planning.
  10. Repeat the process for each feature/function throughout the iteration cycle.
Accessibility & Usability
  • Conduct accessibility compliance testing of the solution within each iteration.
  • Conduct regular usability testing sessions on the MVP.
  • Use findings from testing to continuously improve the product/service.
Phase 4 – Live
Live focuses on continuous improvement after the service reaches maturity and its core features have been implemented.
Responsibilities & Deliverables
Continue facilitating user research activities, including:
  • User Interview Topic Maps
  • User Interview Scripts
  • User Interview Synthesis
  • User Research Findings Reports
Additionally:
  • Conduct regular accessibility compliance testing of the live build as improvements are released.
  • Conduct regular usability testing on the live product/service.
  • Analyze usage analytics and user behaviour patterns.
  • Track and measure KPIs.
  • Use research, analytics, and testing insights to continuously improve the service.
Ideal Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate is a Senior UX Designer with strong hands-on experience across the full product/service design lifecycle, rather than someone focused solely on visual/UI design.
The candidate should be able to demonstrate experience with:
User Research → Discovery → Personas/Stakeholder Mapping → Journey/User Flows → Prototyping → Usability Testing → Iteration → Accessibility → Agile/Scrum → User Stories → MVP/Beta → Live/Continuous Improvement
Candidates with experience delivering government/public-sector digital services and familiarity with the Ontario Digital Service Design Playbook will be particularly well aligned.
Recruiter Screening Checklist
Before submission, confirm the candidate can clearly demonstrate:
  • Extensive UX design best-practice experience
  • Mobile-first design – Mandatory
  • Responsive design – Mandatory
  • 3+ years on complex projects/products – Mandatory
  • User-centred design experience
  • Agile/Scrum experience – Mandatory
  • Communication and mediation with business/core teams – Mandatory
  • Ability to keep projects/products progressing according to schedule
  • User research facilitation
  • User interviews
  • Interview topic maps
  • Interview scripts
  • Interview synthesis
  • User research findings reports

title: Customer Experience Coordinator (Part-Time) - Orange, CT
description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As a Customer Experience Coordinator, your job is to define the customer’s experience through service, focus, and participation—so you are passionate about perfecting the experience before, during, and after their time at VEG. Outgoing and personable, with each customer, you conduct yourself professionally in both demeanor and presence. You find ways to say YES and put pets and customers experience above all else. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to grow where you want to go, building valuable experience and paving the way for your career to take unexpected and rewarding directions.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Greet every customer with warmth and urgency, whether in person, over the phone, or online
  • Oversee all customer communications (calls, emails, texts), record details accurately, and route urgent medical calls to a doctor quickly
  • Deliver personalized, memorable experiences—always looking for creative ways to say “yes” to customer needs
  • Listen with empathy, resolve concerns quickly, and anticipate issues before they escalate
  • Keep nursing team and doctors updated on customer needs for a seamless care experience.
  • Provide confidential, compassionate guidance on financial options and end-of-life decisions
  • Process payments accurately while protecting personal and financial information.
  • Follow up with customers after visits to check on their pet’s care and strengthen relationships
  • Celebrate and capture special moments (with permission), creating lasting connections between customers, their pets, and the hospital

WHAT YOU NEED

  • 2+ years of experience in a customer service role
  • Advanced proficiency in computer programs and practice management software
  • Highly organized, with strong attention to detail
  • Strong communication skills; able to interact positively with anyone and everyone
  • The ability to multitask and thrive amid chaos
  • High emotional intelligence, able to read a room and plan and act accordingly
  • Adaptable and amenable in high stakes environments
  • Problem solving skills and a focus on innovation
  • Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors
  • Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs
  • Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

  • Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives
  • Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments
  • Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results
  • Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

  • Competitive compensation ($18.00 - $26.00/hr)
  • A BIG focus on learning and growth from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to Unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (No really!). Part-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend. Part-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $400/year travel stipend.
  • Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work
  • Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people
  • And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

title: Specification Lead, Quality Operations
description:
Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq ARWR) is a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company that develops medicines that treat intractable diseases by silencing the genes that cause them. Using a broad portfolio of RNA chemistries and efficient modes of delivery, Arrowhead therapies trigger the RNA interference mechanism to induce rapid, deep, and durable knockdown of target genes. RNA interference, or RNAi, is a mechanism present in living cells that inhibits the expression of a specific gene, thereby affecting the production of a specific protein. Arrowhead’s RNAi-based therapeutics leverage this natural pathway of gene silencing.

Arrowhead is focused on developing innovative drugs for diseases with a genetic basis, typically characterized by the overproduction of one or more proteins that are involved with disease. The depth and versatility of our RNAi technologies enables us to potentially address conditions in virtually any therapeutic area and pursue disease targets that are not otherwise addressable by small molecules and biologics. Arrowhead is leading the field in bringing the promise of RNAi to address diseases outside of the liver, and our clinical pipeline includes disease targets in the liver and lung with a promising pipeline of preclinical candidates.

Arrowhead’s corporate headquarters is in Pasadena, CA with research and development teams in Madison, WI & San Diego, CA, and a state of the art manufacturing facility in Verona, WI. Our employees are nimble, science-driven innovators who are collaborating to bring new therapies to patients in need.

The Position

This position resides within the Integrated Quality Operations team and serves as the owner of the specification lifecycle for Arrowhead's product portfolio, from early phase clinical development, through late phase clinical, and commercial supply. The Specification Lead is responsible for the creation, review, approval, revision, periodic review, and version control of specifications for intermediates, drug substance, drug product, and finished goods, and for ensuring that there is agreement on and justification that the acceptance criteria are phase-appropriate, justified, tighten appropriately as programs progress, and remain aligned with filed commitments and compendial requirements. The Specification Lead works closely with Analytical and Process Development, Quality Control, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the Quality owner of the specification lifecycle for intermediates, drug substance, drug product, and finished goods across clinical and commercial programs.
  • Author, review, and route specifications for approval, and maintain version control, effective dating, and distribution within the electronic document management system.
  • Ensure acceptance criteria are phase-appropriate and scientifically justified, working collaboratively with Analytical and Process Development, Quality Control, CMC, and Regulatory Affairs as criteria are established and tightened from early phase through process validation and commercial supply.
  • Maintain alignment between approved specifications and registered or filed commitments (IND/CTA/IMPD and NDA/BLA/MAA), and ensure specification changes are assessed for regulatory impact and filing requirements prior to implementation.
  • Maintain alignment with compendial requirements (USP, Ph. Eur., JP), monitor compendial forecasts and revisions, and support the assessment of the impact of monograph and general chapter changes on specifications and associated test methods.
  • Lead periodic review of specifications on the defined cycle, including verification of current test methods, references, acceptance criteria, and regulatory and compendial alignment.
  • Own specification change controls, including impact assessment, coordination of downstream actions (test method and procedural document updates, certificate of analysis templates, batch record and label updates), and verification of implementation.
  • Maintain the specification index and ensure traceability between specifications, test methods, reference standards, and material and product codes.
  • Support new program onboarding and technical transfer by establishing initial specifications for new materials, intermediates, and products.
  • Track and report specification program metrics, including on-time completion of periodic reviews, open specification change controls, and record aging.
  • Maintain inspection readiness for the specification program and serve as the subject matter expert for specification related questions during audits and health authority inspections.
  • Write, review, update, and issue applicable Procedural Documents governing specification creation, revision, periodic review, and compendial monitoring.
  • Collaborate with, and provide quality support for, other departments (Analytical Development/QC, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Project Management, etc.).
  • Maintain knowledge of current compliance expectations and regulations pertaining to specifications and analytical testing (e.g., 21 CFR Parts 210/211, ICH Q1A(R2), Q2(R2), Q3A/Q3B, Q3C/Q3D, and Q6A/Q6B, and USP/Ph. Eur. compendial requirements).
  • Other duties consistent with the position as assigned from time to time.

Requirements

  • Bachelors Degree in Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, or a related scientific field
  • 5+ years of pharmaceutical or biotechnology experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Control, or Analytical Development, including direct experience with specifications and analytical test methods.
  • Demonstrated experience authoring, revising, and approving specifications for raw materials, drug substance, and/or drug product.
  • Working knowledge of compendial requirements (USP, Ph. Eur., JP) and their application to specifications and test methods.
  • Working knowledge of analytical methods and data sufficient to evaluate acceptance criteria, reporting conventions, and method suitability.
  • Experience with change control and document control within a GMP environment.
  • Working knowledge of US and international GMP regulations and ICH guidance applicable to investigational and commercial products, including phase-appropriate acceptance criteria.
  • Excellent attention to detail and demonstrated ability to manage a high volume of controlled documents accurately.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work with diverse professionals across quality, analytical, regulatory, and manufacturing functions.
  • Highly motivated team player willing to contribute to a growing pharmaceutical organization.
  • A detail-oriented self-starter who endeavors to anticipate and resolve problems and seeks opportunities to grow their role and responsibilities at Arrowhead.

Preferred

  • Advanced degree in a science field.
  • Experience supporting an NDA/BLA/MAA submission, including preparation or justification of specifications.
  • Experience managing specifications through the transition from early phase into late phase and commercial supply.
  • Experience with compendial change monitoring and assessment of monograph and general chapter revisions.
  • Experience configuring or verifying specifications within LIMS and/or ERP systems.
  • Experience applying statistical evaluation of manufacturing and analytical data to support setting of acceptance criteria.
  • Experience with sterile/parenteral drug product and with oligonucleotide, peptide, or biologic modalities.
  • Experience with electronic quality management and document control systems (e.g., Veeva Vault, TrackWise, MasterControl).
  • Additional Quality/Regulatory related certification desired, such as CQA, CQE, RAC, etc.
Wisconsin pay range
$90,000—$105,000 USD

Arrowhead provides competitive salaries and an excellent benefit package.

Candidates must have current, valid authorization to work in the country where this role is located.
